title.zh: 卷44 羅結 伊馛 乙瑰 和其奴 苟頽 薛野𧗠者 宇文福 費于 孟威
title.en: Volume 44: Luo Jie, Yi Bo, Yi Gui, He Qinu, Gou Tui, Xueye Zhe, Yuwen Fu, Fei Yu, Meng Wei
title.raw: 卷44 羅結 伊馛 乙瑰 和其奴 苟頽 薛野𧗠者 宇文福 費于 孟威 Volume 44: Luo Jie, Yi Bo, Yi Gui, He Qinu, Gou Tui, Xueye Zhe, Yuwen Fu, Fei Yu, Meng Wei

sentences.zh: 羅結 伊馛 乙瓌 和其奴 苟頹 薛野䐗 宇文福 費于 孟威

translations.literal: Luo Jie, Yi Bo, Yi Gui, He Qinu, Gou Tui, Xueye Zhe, Yuwen Fu, Fei Yu, Meng Wei
translations.idiomatic: Luo Jie, Yi Bo, Yi Gui, He Qinu, Gou Tui, Xueye Zhe, Yuwen Fu, Fei Yu, and Meng Wei

sentences.zh: 羅結，代人也，其先世領部落，為國附臣。

translations.literal: Luo Jie was a man of Dai. His ancestors for generations led their tribe and were vassal subjects of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Jie was a native of Dai. For generations his forebears had led their tribe and served the state as attached subjects.

sentences.zh: 劉顯之謀逆也，太祖去之。

translations.literal: When Liu Xian plotted rebellion, Taizu went to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xian plotted treason, Taizu marched against him.

sentences.zh: 結翼衞鑾輿，從幸賀蘭部。

translations.literal: Jie winged the imperial carriage on both sides and followed in attendance on the Helan tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Jie flanked the imperial carriage and accompanied the court to the Helan tribe.

sentences.zh: 後以功賜爵屈蛇侯。

translations.literal: Later, for merit he was granted the title Marquis of Qushe.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for his achievements he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qushe.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，除持節、散騎常侍、寧南將軍、河內鎮將。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Mingyuan, he was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the South, and Garrison Commander of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mingyuan he was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the South, and Garrison Commander of Henei.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，遷侍中、外都大官，總三十六曹事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizu's reign, he was transferred to Palace Attendant and Grand Officer of the Outer Court, overseeing the affairs of the thirty-six bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shizu's reign he was promoted to Palace Attendant and Grand Officer of the Outer Court, with overall charge of the thirty-six bureaus.

sentences.zh: 年一百七歲，精爽不衰。

translations.literal: At the age of one hundred and seven, his spirit remained undiminished.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of one hundred and seven his vigor of mind had not waned.

sentences.zh: 世祖以其忠慤，甚見信待，監典後宮，出入臥內，因除長信卿。

translations.literal: Shizu, because of his loyalty and earnestness, greatly trusted and favored him, put him in charge of the rear palace, and allowed him to enter and leave the sleeping quarters; he was therefore appointed Director of Changxin.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu, finding him loyal and steadfast, trusted him deeply, placed him in charge of the rear palace, and allowed him free access to the inner apartments; he was then appointed Director of Changxin.

sentences.zh: 年一百一十，詔聽歸老，賜大寧東川以為居業，并為築城，即號曰羅侯城，至今猶存。

translations.literal: At the age of one hundred and ten, an edict permitted him to retire; he was granted Daning's eastern stream as his residence and estate, and a city was built for him, which was called Luohou City and still exists today.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of one hundred and ten he was permitted by edict to retire. He was granted the eastern stream of Daning as his home estate, and a walled settlement was built for him that was named Luohou City; it still stands today.

sentences.zh: 朝廷每有大事，驛馬詢訪焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the court had a major affair, relay horses were sent to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court faced a weighty matter, couriers were dispatched to seek his counsel.

sentences.zh: 年一百二十歲，卒。

translations.literal: At the age of one hundred and twenty he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of one hundred and twenty.

sentences.zh: 贈寧東將軍、幽州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of You Province; posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of You Province, with the posthumous title Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子斤，太宗時為侍御中散。

translations.literal: His son Jin, in the time of Emperor Mingyuan, served as Attendant of the Imperial Guard and Central Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin served under Emperor Mingyuan as Attendant of the Imperial Guard and Central Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 後從世祖討赫連昌，世祖追奔入城，昌邀擊，左右多死，斤力戰有功。

translations.literal: Later he followed Shizu in campaigning against Helian Chang. Shizu pursued the enemy in flight into the city; Chang intercepted and struck, and many of those around the emperor were killed, but Jin fought fiercely with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Shizu in the campaign against Helian Chang. Shizu pursued the foe into the city; Chang counterattacked, and many of those around the emperor were killed, yet Jin fought hard and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉之。

translations.literal: Shizu commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 後錄勳，除散騎常侍、侍中、四部尚書，又加平西將軍。

translations.literal: Later, when merits were recorded, he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Palace Attendant, and Director of the Four Departments, and additionally made General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: When merits were later tallied, he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Palace Attendant, and Director of the Four Departments, and was further made General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 後平涼州，攻城野戰，多有克捷，以功賜爵帶方公，除長安鎮都大將。

translations.literal: Later he pacified Liang Province; in storming cities and fighting in the field he won many victories, and for merit was granted the title Duke of Daifang and appointed Grand Garrison Commander of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He later helped pacify Liang Province; in sieges and field battles he won repeated victories, and for his merit was enfeoffed as Duke of Daifang and appointed Grand Garrison Commander of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 會蠕蠕侵境，馳驛徵還，除柔玄鎮都大將。

translations.literal: When the Rouran invaded the borders, he was summoned back by relay and appointed Grand Garrison Commander of Rouxuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran raided the frontier, he was recalled by urgent dispatch and appointed Grand Garrison Commander of Rouxuan.

sentences.zh: 後以斤機辯，敕與王俊使蠕蠕，迎女備後宮。

translations.literal: Later, because Jin was resourceful and eloquent, he was ordered together with Wang Jun to go as envoy to the Rouran and bring back a princess for the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because Jin was quick-witted and articulate, he was ordered with Wang Jun to go as envoys to the Rouran and bring back a princess for the rear palace.

sentences.zh: 又以本將軍開府，為長安鎮都大將。

translations.literal: Again, with his original rank he opened a headquarters and served as Grand Garrison Commander of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He again held his former rank with an opened headquarters as Grand Garrison Commander of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈本將軍、雍州刺史，諡曰靜，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed to his former generalship and made Inspector of Yong Province, with posthumous title Jing; he was buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously confirmed in his former generalship and made Inspector of Yong Province, with the posthumous title Jing; he was buried with honor at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 子敦，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Dun inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dun inherited the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 有姿貌，善舉止。

translations.literal: He had a handsome appearance and graceful bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He was handsome in appearance and graceful in deportment.

sentences.zh: 自太子洗馬稍遷散騎常侍、庫部尚書。

translations.literal: From Groom of the Heir Apparent he was gradually promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Director of the Storehouse Department.
translations.idiomatic: From Groom of the Heir Apparent he rose by stages to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Director of the Storehouse Department.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈安東將軍、幽州刺史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of You Province, with posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of You Province, with the posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 子伊利，高宗時襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yili, in the time of Emperor Wencheng, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yili inherited the title in the reign of Emperor Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 除內行長，以沉密小心、恭勤不怠領御食、羽獵諸曹事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief of the Inner Service and, for his deep reserve, carefulness, respectful diligence, and untiring service, was put in charge of the imperial kitchens, hunting with feathered arrows, and other offices.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Chief of the Inner Service and, for his discretion, carefulness, and tireless dutifulness, was placed in charge of the imperial kitchens, feathered hunts, and related offices.

sentences.zh: 伊利曾病，顯祖幸其宅，自視醫藥，其見待如此。

translations.literal: When Yili once fell ill, Xianzu visited his residence and personally inspected his medicines; such was the favor in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: When Yili fell ill, Xianzu visited his home and personally looked to his medicines; such was the regard in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 稍遷散騎常侍、儀曹尚書，出為安東將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Director of the Ceremonial Bureau, then sent out as General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Director of the Ceremonial Bureau, then sent out as General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 善撫導，在州數年，邊民歸之五千餘戶。

translations.literal: Skilled in comforting and guiding the people, during several years in the province more than five thousand border households submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in winning and guiding people, during several years in the province more than five thousand frontier households came under his authority.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，蠕蠕來寇，詔伊利追擊之，不及而反。

translations.literal: In the time of Gaozu, when the Rouran came raiding, an edict ordered Yili to pursue them; he failed to overtake them and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaozu's reign, when the Rouran raided, Yili was ordered to pursue them; he could not catch them and turned back.

sentences.zh: 後依例降為侯。

translations.literal: Later, according to precedent, his rank was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Later, by the usual rule, his rank was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 除司農卿、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Directorate of Agriculture and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Directorate of Agriculture and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，贈征北將軍、燕州刺史，諡曰靜。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, he was posthumously appointed General Who Campaigns North and Inspector of Yan Province, with posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was posthumously appointed General Who Campaigns North and Inspector of Yan Province, with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 子阿奴，亦忠實寡言，有智度。

translations.literal: His son Anu was likewise loyal, trustworthy, sparing of words, and possessed of judgment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Anu was likewise loyal, trustworthy, sparing of speech, and possessed of judgment.

sentences.zh: 以勳臣之子，除侍御中散，襲爵。

translations.literal: As the son of a meritorious minister, he was appointed Attendant of the Imperial Guard and Central Scattered Cavalry and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: As the son of a meritorious minister, he was appointed Attendant of the Imperial Guard and Central Scattered Cavalry and inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 稍遷中散大夫。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Grand Master of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Grand Master of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子殺鬼，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Shagui inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shagui inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 武泰中，驃騎將軍、南青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Wutai era he was General of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of Southern Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wutai era he was General of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of Southern Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 敦弟拔，歷殿中尚書，賜爵濟南公。

translations.literal: Dun's younger brother Ba served successively as Director of the Palace Secretariat and was granted the title Duke of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's younger brother Ba served as Director of the Palace Secretariat and was granted the title Duke of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，進爵為王。

translations.literal: In the time of Gaozu his rank was advanced to king.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozu his rank was advanced to king.

sentences.zh: 除征西將軍、吏部尚書，改封趙郡王。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Campaigns West and Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and his fief was changed to Prince of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Campaigns West and Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and his fief was changed to Prince of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 後例降為公。

translations.literal: Later, by precedent, he was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Later, by precedent, he was reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈寧東將軍、定州刺史，諡曰康，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ding Province, with posthumous title Kang; he was buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ding Province, with the posthumous title Kang; he was buried with honor at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 子道生，肆州安北府外兵參軍。

translations.literal: His son Daosheng was External Military Registrar of the Anbei Headquarters in Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daosheng was External Military Registrar of the Anbei Headquarters in Si Province.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子延，天興中，驃騎將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His son Yan, in the Tianxing era, was General of Agile Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan, in the Tianxing era, was General of Agile Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

translations.literal: The text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: [1] The text is deficient.

sentences.zh: 結從子渥，渥子提，並歷通顯。

translations.literal: Jie's younger clansman Wo; Wo's son Ti—both rose to high and prominent office.
translations.idiomatic: Jie's younger clansman Wo, and Wo's son Ti, both attained eminent positions.

sentences.zh: 提從世祖討赫連昌有功，賜昌女為妻。

translations.literal: Ti followed Shizu in campaigning against Helian Chang with merit and was given Chang's daughter as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Ti followed Shizu in the campaign against Helian Chang with merit and was given Chang's daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 子雲，早有名位。

translations.literal: His son Yun early gained name and rank.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yun early gained reputation and office.

sentences.zh: 顯祖時給事中，西征敕勒，為賊所襲殺。

translations.literal: In the time of Xianzu he was a Gentleman Attendant-in-Ordinary; on the western campaign against the Tiele he was killed in a bandit attack.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianzu he was Gentleman Attendant-in-Ordinary; on the western expedition against the Tiele he was killed in a rebel attack.

sentences.zh: 子蓋，世宗時右將軍、直閤將軍。

translations.literal: His son Gai, in the time of Emperor Xiaowen, was General of the Right and General of the Direct Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gai, in Emperor Xiaowen's reign, was General of the Right and General of the Direct Gate.

sentences.zh: 轉龍驤將軍、濟州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Dragon Charger and Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of the Dragon Charger and Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈本將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed to his former generalship and made Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously confirmed in his former generalship and made Inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 長子鑒，累遷冠軍將軍、岐州刺史。

translations.literal: His eldest son Jian rose by stages to General Who Overcomes the Enemy and Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Jian rose by stages to General Who Overcomes the Enemy and Inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 入除散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫、主衣都統。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Purse, and Chief of the Imperial Wardrobe.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Purse, and Chief of the Imperial Wardrobe.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈侍中、都督冀定瀛三州諸軍事、尚書右僕射、司空公、衞將軍、冀州刺史，以孝靜外戚故也。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Ji, Ding, and Ying provinces, Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Duke of the Ministry of Works, General of the Guard, and Inspector of Ji Province—because he was a maternal relative of Emperor Xiaojing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Ji, Ding, and Ying provinces, Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Duke of the Ministry of Works, General of the Guard, and Inspector of Ji Province—because he was a maternal kinsman of Emperor Xiaojing.

sentences.zh: 鑒弟衡，累遷天水、樂陵二郡太守，輔國將軍，光州刺史。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Heng rose by stages to Administrator of the two commanderies of Tianshui and Leling, General Who Assists the State, and Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Heng rose by stages to Administrator of Tianshui and Leling, General Who Assists the State, and Inspector of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 結宗人彌，善射有膂力。

translations.literal: Jie's clansman Mi was skilled at archery and possessed great strength.
translations.idiomatic: Jie's clansman Mi was skilled in archery and possessed great physical strength.

sentences.zh: 世祖時為軍將，數從征伐有功，官至范陽太守。

translations.literal: In the time of Shizu he was a military officer; he followed campaigns many times with merit and rose to Administrator of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizu he was a military officer; he took part in many campaigns with merit and rose to Administrator of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈幽州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed Inspector of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Inspector of You Province.

sentences.zh: 彌孫念，字子懷。

translations.literal: Mi's grandson Nian, styled Zihuai.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's grandson Nian, styled Zihuai.

sentences.zh: 武定中，驃騎將軍、膠州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he was General of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he was General of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of Jiao Province.

sentences.zh: 伊馛，代人也。

translations.literal: Yi Bo was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Bo was a native of Dai.

sentences.zh: 少而勇健，走及奔馬，善射，多力，曳牛却行。

translations.literal: From youth he was brave and robust; he could run as fast as a galloping horse, was skilled at archery, possessed great strength, and could drag an ox backward while walking.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was brave and hardy; he could keep pace with a galloping horse, excelled at archery, possessed great strength, and could walk backward while dragging an ox.

sentences.zh: 神䴥初，擢為侍郎，轉三郎，賜爵汾陽子，加振威將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlu era he was promoted to Attendant, then transferred to Third-Rank Attendant, granted the title Marquis of Fenyang, and made General Who Shakes Might.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlu era he was promoted to Attendant, then transferred to Third-Rank Attendant, enfeoffed as Marquis of Fenyang, and made General Who Shakes Might.

sentences.zh: 世祖之將討涼州也，議者咸諫，唯司徒崔浩勸世祖決行。

translations.literal: When Shizu was about to campaign against Liang Province, the advisers all remonstrated; only Minister of Works Cui Hao urged Shizu to decide on the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu was preparing to campaign against Liang Province, the advisers all remonstrated; only Minister of Works Cui Hao urged Shizu to commit to the expedition.

sentences.zh: 羣臣出後，馛言於世祖曰：「若涼州無水草，何得為國？

translations.literal: After the ministers had withdrawn, Bo said to Shizu: "If Liang Province lacked grass and water, how could it sustain a state?
translations.idiomatic: After the ministers had withdrawn, Bo said to Shizu: "If Liang Province lacked grass and water, how could it have become a state?

sentences.zh: 議者不可用也，宜從浩言。

translations.literal: The advisers cannot be followed; Your Majesty should heed Hao's words.
translations.idiomatic: The advisers cannot be followed; Your Majesty should heed Hao's counsel.

sentences.zh: 」世祖善之。

translations.literal: " Shizu approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Shizu approved.

sentences.zh: 既克涼州，世祖大會於姑臧，謂羣臣曰：「崔公智計有餘，吾亦不復奇之。

translations.literal: After Liang Province had been taken, Shizu held a great assembly at Guzang and said to the ministers: "Master Cui's stratagems are more than sufficient; I am no longer surprised by them.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang Province was taken, Shizu held a great assembly at Guzang and said to the ministers: "Master Cui's stratagems are more than sufficient; I am no longer surprised by them.

sentences.zh: 吾正奇馛弓馬之士，而所見能與崔同，此深自可奇。

translations.literal: What I truly marvel at is Bo, a master of bow and horse, whose insight can match Cui's—this is deeply remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: What I truly marvel at is Bo, a master of bow and horse, whose insight can match Cui's—this is deeply remarkable.

sentences.zh: 」顧謂浩曰：「馛智力如此，終至公相。

translations.literal: " Turning to Hao he said: "With intelligence such as Bo's, he will in the end reach the rank of duke or minister.
translations.idiomatic: " Turning to Hao he said: "With intelligence such as Bo's, he will in the end reach the rank of duke or minister.

sentences.zh: 」浩曰：「何必讀書，然後為學。

translations.literal: " Hao said: "Why must one read books before learning becomes possible.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao said: "Why must one read books before learning becomes possible.

sentences.zh: 衞青、霍去病亦不讀書，而能大建勳名，致位公輔。

translations.literal: Wei Qing and Huo Qubing also did not read books, yet they could build great merit and reach the highest offices.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qing and Huo Qubing also did not read books, yet they could build great merit and reach the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 」世祖笑曰：「誠如公言。」

translations.literal: " Shizu laughed and said: "It is indeed as you say."
translations.idiomatic: " Shizu laughed and said: "It is indeed as you say."

sentences.zh: 子蘭，襲。

translations.literal: His son Lan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍、庫部尚書。

translations.literal: Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Director of the Storehouse Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Director of the Storehouse Department.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子盆生，驍勇有膽氣。

translations.literal: His son Pensheng was fierce and brave and possessed daring.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pensheng was fierce and brave and possessed daring.

sentences.zh: 初為統軍，累有戰功，遂為名將。

translations.literal: At first he was a commander-in-chief; he accumulated battle achievements and thus became a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was a commander-in-chief; he accumulated battle achievements and thus became a famous general.

sentences.zh: 以勳賜爵平城子。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted the title Viscount of Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 神龜二年，自驍騎將軍、直閤將軍為持節、右將軍、洛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengui, from General of Agile Cavalry and General of the Direct Gate he became Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General of the Right, and Inspector of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengui he rose from General of Agile Cavalry and General of the Direct Gate to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General of the Right, and Inspector of Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 與荊州刺史、淮南王世遵，魯陽太守崔模俱討襄陽，不克而還，坐免官。

translations.literal: Together with the Inspector of Jing Province, Prince of Huainan Shizun, and the Administrator of Luyang Cui Mo he attacked Xiangyang, failed to take it, and returned; he was dismissed from office for the fault.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the Inspector of Jing Province, Prince of Huainan Shizun, and the Administrator of Luyang Cui Mo he attacked Xiangyang, failed to take it, and returned; he was dismissed from office on that account.

sentences.zh: 後除安西將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 又為撫軍將軍、太僕卿、假鎮西將軍、西道別將，每戰頻捷。

translations.literal: Again he was made General Who Pacifies the Army, Grand Minister of the Imperial Stud, Acting General Who Campaigns West, and Separate Commander of the Western Route; in every battle he won repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made General Who Pacifies the Army, Grand Minister of the Imperial Stud, Acting General Who Campaigns West, and Separate Commander of the Western Route; in every battle he won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 自崔延伯之後，盆生為次焉。

translations.literal: After Cui Yanbo, Pensheng was second among them.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Yanbo, Pensheng ranked second among them.

sentences.zh: 進號征西將軍，行岐州刺史。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Campaigns West, and he acted as Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: His title was advanced to General Who Campaigns West, and he acted as Inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 復為西道都督，戰歿。

translations.literal: Again he was made Commander-in-Chief of the Western Route and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Commander-in-Chief of the Western Route and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈車騎將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，重贈驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、定州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he was again posthumously appointed Grand General of Agile Cavalry, with the same ceremonial privileges as the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era he was again posthumously appointed Grand General of Agile Cavalry, with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 子武平，司徒祭酒。

translations.literal: His son Wuping was Libationer of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wuping was Libationer of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 武平弟武榮，直閤將軍。

translations.literal: Wuping's younger brother Wurong was General of the Direct Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wuping's younger brother Wurong was General of the Direct Gate.

sentences.zh: 馛族孫豹子，武衞將軍。

translations.literal: Bo's clansman's grandson Baozi was General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Bo's clansman's grandson Baozi was General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 豹子從子琳，亦武衞將軍。

translations.literal: Baozi's younger clansman Lin was also General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi's younger clansman Lin was also General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 乙瓌，代人也。

translations.literal: Yi Gui was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Gui was a native of Dai.

sentences.zh: 其先世統部落。

translations.literal: His ancestors for generations had ruled the tribe.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors for generations had ruled the tribe.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，瓌父匹知慕國威化，遣瓌入貢，世祖因留之。

translations.literal: In the time of Shizu, Gui's father Pizhi, admiring the state's majesty and civilizing influence, sent Gui to present tribute; Shizu therefore detained him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizu, Gui's father Pizhi, admiring the state's majesty and civilizing power, sent Gui to present tribute; Shizu therefore kept him at court.

sentences.zh: 瓌便弓馬，善射，手格猛獸，膂力過人。

translations.literal: Gui was skilled with bow and horse, excelled at archery, could grapple fierce beasts with his hands, and his strength surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was skilled with bow and horse, excelled at archery, could grapple fierce beasts with his bare hands, and his strength surpassed ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 數從征伐，甚見信待。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns many times and was greatly trusted and favored.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in many campaigns and was greatly trusted and favored.

sentences.zh: 尚上谷公主，世祖之女也。

translations.literal: He married Princess Shanggu, a daughter of Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Shanggu, a daughter of Shizu.

sentences.zh: 除鎮南將軍、駙馬都尉，賜爵西平公。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Guards the South and Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law and granted the title Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Guards the South and Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law and enfeoffed as Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 從駕南征，除使持節、都督前鋒諸軍事。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial procession on the southern expedition and was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Commander-in-Chief of the vanguard forces.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the southern expedition and was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Commander-in-Chief of the vanguard forces.

sentences.zh: 每戰，身先士卒，勇冠三軍。

translations.literal: In every battle he took the lead among the soldiers and his bravery topped the three armies.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle he led from the front and his courage topped the three armies.

sentences.zh: 後除侍中、征東將軍、儀同三司、定州刺史，進爵為王。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Palace Attendant, General Who Campaigns East, with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Ding Province, and his rank was advanced to king.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Palace Attendant, General Who Campaigns East, with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Ding Province, and his rank was advanced to king.

sentences.zh: 又為西道都將。

translations.literal: He was again made Commander of the Western Route.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Commander of the Western Route.

sentences.zh: [2]和平中薨，時年二十九。

translations.literal: [2] In the Heping era he died; he was then twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: [2] In the Heping era he died; he was then twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉公，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed Duke of the Ministry of Works, with posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Duke of the Ministry of Works, with the posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 子海，字懷仁。

translations.literal: His son Hai, styled Huairen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hai, styled Huairen.

sentences.zh: 少歷侍御中散、散騎侍郎，卒時年四十一。

translations.literal: From youth he served as Attendant of the Imperial Guard and Central Scattered Cavalry and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; he died at the age of forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he served as Attendant of the Imperial Guard and Central Scattered Cavalry and as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; he died at the age of forty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、衞將軍、濟州刺史，諡曰孝。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General of the Guard, and Inspector of Ji Province, with posthumous title Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General of the Guard, and Inspector of Ji Province, with the posthumous title Xiao.

sentences.zh: 瑗弟諧，字遵和。

translations.literal: Yuan's younger brother Xie, styled Zunhe.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's younger brother Xie, styled Zunhe.

sentences.zh: 武定中，司馬。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he was a marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he was a marshal.

sentences.zh: 諧弟琛，字仲珍。

translations.literal: Xie's younger brother Chen, styled Zhongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Xie's younger brother Chen, styled Zhongzhen.

sentences.zh: 解褐司空參軍事。

translations.literal: On leaving the purple he was a staff member of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On first taking office he was a staff member of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 稍遷東平、濟陰二郡太守，散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Administrator of the two commanderies of Dongping and Jiyin and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Administrator of Dongping and Jiyin and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 卒時年四十九。

translations.literal: He died at the age of forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 和其奴，代人也。

translations.literal: He Qinu was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He Qinu was a native of Dai.

sentences.zh: 少有操行，善射御。

translations.literal: From youth he possessed conduct and integrity and was skilled at archery and charioteering.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he possessed integrity of conduct and was skilled at archery and charioteering.

sentences.zh: 初為三郎，轉羽林中郎，以恭勤致稱。

translations.literal: At first he was a Third-Rank Attendant, then transferred to Captain of the Feathered Forest, and won praise for respectful diligence.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was a Third-Rank Attendant, then transferred to Captain of the Feathered Forest, and won praise for respectful diligence.

sentences.zh: 賜爵東陽子，除奮武將軍。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Marquis of Dongyang and appointed General Who Inspires Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongyang and appointed General Who Inspires Martiality.

sentences.zh: 高宗初，[4]遷尚書，加散騎常侍，進爵平昌公，拜安南將軍，遷尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wencheng's reign, [4] he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Secretariat, made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, advanced to Duke of Pingchang, appointed General Who Pacifies the South, and transferred to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Wencheng's reign, [4] he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Secretariat, made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, advanced to Duke of Pingchang, appointed General Who Pacifies the South, and transferred to Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太安元年，詔羣臣議立皇太子名。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taian, an edict ordered the ministers to discuss the name of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taian, an edict ordered the ministers to discuss the name of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 其奴與司徒麗等以為宜以德命名，帝從之。

translations.literal: Qinu together with Minister of Works Li and others held that the name should be chosen for virtue; the emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Qinu together with Minister of Works Li and others held that the name should be chosen for virtue; the emperor followed this.

sentences.zh: 又與河東王閭毗、太宰常英等並平尚書事。

translations.literal: Again, together with Prince of Hedong Lu Pi, Grand Preceptor Chang Ying, and others he jointly oversaw the affairs of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He again, together with Prince of Hedong Lu Pi, Grand Preceptor Chang Ying, and others, jointly oversaw the affairs of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 在官慎法，不受私請。

translations.literal: In office he was careful of the law and did not accept private requests.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was careful of the law and did not accept private requests.

sentences.zh: 時以西征吐谷渾諸將淹停不進，久囚未決。

translations.literal: At that time, because the generals on the western expedition against Tuyuhun had halted and not advanced, they had long been imprisoned without decision.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the generals on the western expedition against Tuyuhun had halted and not advanced, and had long been imprisoned without a decision.

sentences.zh: 其奴與尚書毛法仁等窮問其狀連日，具伏。

translations.literal: Qinu together with Director of the Imperial Secretariat Mao Faren and others questioned their circumstances day after day until all confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Qinu together with Director Mao Faren and others questioned their circumstances day after day until all confessed.

sentences.zh: 和平六年，遷司空，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Heping he was transferred to Minister of Works and made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Heping he was transferred to Minister of Works and made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，乙渾與林金閭擅殺尚書楊保年等。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wencheng died, Yi Hun together with Lin Jinlu arbitrarily killed Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yang Baonian and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng died, Yi Hun together with Lin Jinlu arbitrarily killed Director of the Imperial Secretariat Yang Baonian and others.

sentences.zh: 殿中尚書元郁率殿中宿衞士欲加兵於渾。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Secretariat Yuan Yu led the palace guards and intended to apply armed force against Hun.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Palace Secretariat Yuan Yu led the palace guards and intended to apply armed force against Hun.

sentences.zh: 渾懼，歸咎於金閭，執金閭以付郁。

translations.literal: Hun was afraid and shifted the blame onto Jinlu, seized Jinlu, and handed him over to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Hun was afraid and shifted the blame onto Jinlu, seized Jinlu, and handed him over to Yu.

sentences.zh: 時其奴以金閭罪惡未分，乃出之為定州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Qinu, because Jinlu's guilt had not yet been determined, released him and sent him out as Inspector of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qinu, because Jinlu's guilt had not yet been determined, released him and sent him out as Inspector of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 皇興元年，長安鎮將東平王道符反，詔其奴領征西大將軍，率殿中精甲萬騎以討之，未至而道符敗，軍還。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangxing, when the Garrison Commander of Chang'an, Prince of Dongping Daofu, rebelled, an edict ordered Qinu to lead the campaign as General Who Campaigns West, at the head of ten thousand picked cavalry of the palace guard to suppress him; before he arrived Daofu had already been defeated, and the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangxing, when the Garrison Commander of Chang'an, Prince of Dongping Daofu, rebelled, an edict ordered Qinu to lead the campaign as General Who Campaigns West at the head of ten thousand picked palace cavalry; before he arrived Daofu had already been defeated, and the army returned.

sentences.zh: 三年薨，內外咸歎惜之。

translations.literal: In the third year he died; inside and outside the court all lamented him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died; court and country alike lamented him.

sentences.zh: 贈平昌王，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed Prince of Pingchang, with posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Prince of Pingchang, with the posthumous title Xuan.

sentences.zh: 子天受，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Tianshou inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tianshou inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 初為內行令。

translations.literal: At first he was Chief of the Inner Service.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was Chief of the Inner Service.

sentences.zh: 太和六年，遷弩庫曹下大夫，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe he was transferred to Junior Master of the Crossbow Storehouse and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taihe he was transferred to Junior Master of the Crossbow Storehouse and died.

sentences.zh: 頹方正好直言，雖文明太后生殺不允，頹亦言至懇切，未曾阿諛。

translations.literal: Tui was by nature fond of speaking frankly; even when the Wenming Empress Dowager would not permit life or death, Tui still spoke with utmost earnestness and never flattered.
translations.idiomatic: Tui was by nature fond of speaking frankly; even when the Wenming Empress Dowager would not permit life or death, Tui still spoke with utmost earnestness and never flattered.

sentences.zh: 李訢、李敷之誅也，[6]頹並致諫，太后不從。

translations.literal: When Li Xin and Li Fu were executed, [6] Tui also remonstrated, but the Empress Dowager did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xin and Li Fu were executed, [6] Tui also remonstrated, but the Empress Dowager did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷征北大將軍、司空公，進爵河東王。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to General Who Campaigns North, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and advanced to Prince of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to General Who Campaigns North, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and advanced to Prince of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 以舊老，聽乘步挽，杖於朝。

translations.literal: As an elder of long service, he was permitted to ride in a hand-drawn carriage and use a staff at court.
translations.idiomatic: As an elder of long service, he was permitted to ride in a hand-drawn carriage and use a staff at court.

sentences.zh: 大駕行幸三川，頹留守京師，沙門法秀謀反，頹率禁衞收掩畢獲，內外晏然。

translations.literal: When the imperial procession traveled to Sanchuan, Tui remained to guard the capital; the monk Faxiu plotted rebellion, and Tui led the palace guard to seize and capture them all; inside and outside were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession traveled to Sanchuan, Tui remained to guard the capital; the monk Faxiu plotted rebellion, and Tui led the palace guard to seize and capture them all, so that inside and outside were tranquil.

sentences.zh: 駕還飲至，文明太后曰：「當爾之日，卿若持疑不即收捕，處分失所，則事成不測矣。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned and held the victory feast, the Wenming Empress Dowager said: "On that day, if you had hesitated and not immediately seized and arrested them, and your disposition had been misplaced, the affair would have become unpredictable.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned and held the victory feast, the Wenming Empress Dowager said: "On that day, if you had hesitated and not immediately seized and arrested them, and your disposition had been misplaced, the affair would have become unpredictable.

sentences.zh: 今京畿不擾，宗社獲安者，實卿之功也。

translations.literal: That the capital region is now undisturbed and the altars of state secure is truly your achievement.
translations.idiomatic: That the capital region is now undisturbed and the altars of state secure is truly your achievement.

sentences.zh: 」七年，詔曰：「頹為台鼎，論道是寄，歷奉四朝，庸績彌遠。

translations.literal: " In the seventh year an edict said: "Tui stands as the state's pillar; the charge of guiding policy rests on him. He has served four reigns, and his ordinary achievements grow ever more distant.
translations.idiomatic: " In the seventh year an edict said: "Tui stands as the state's pillar; the charge of guiding policy rests on him. He has served four reigns, and his ordinary achievements grow ever more distant.

sentences.zh: 宜加崇異，以彰厥功。

translations.literal: He should receive added extraordinary honors to manifest his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He should receive added extraordinary honors to manifest his achievements.

sentences.zh: 自茲已後，可永受復除。

translations.literal: From this time forward he may permanently enjoy exemption from corvée.
translations.idiomatic: From this time forward he may permanently enjoy exemption from corvée.

sentences.zh: 」十三年冬薨。

translations.literal: " In the thirteenth year, winter, he died.
translations.idiomatic: " In the thirteenth year, winter, he died.

sentences.zh: 高祖痛悼者久之。

translations.literal: Gaozu mourned him for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu mourned him for a long time.

sentences.zh: 贈賵有加，諡僖王。

translations.literal: Funeral gifts were increased; posthumous title Prince Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral gifts were increased; his posthumous title was Prince Xi.

sentences.zh: 長子愷，累遷冠軍將軍，柔玄、懷荒、武川鎮大將，襲爵河東王，例降為公。

translations.literal: His eldest son Kai rose by stages to General Who Overcomes the Enemy, Grand Garrison Commander of Rouxuan, Huaihuang, and Wuchuan, inherited the title Prince of Hedong, and by precedent was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Kai rose by stages to General Who Overcomes the Enemy and Grand Garrison Commander of Rouxuan, Huaihuang, and Wuchuan, inherited the title Prince of Hedong, and by precedent was reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 正光二年卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguang he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenguang he died.

sentences.zh: 贈平北將軍、恒州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Heng Province.

sentences.zh: 子寶，武定中，北梁太守。

translations.literal: His son Bao, in the Wuding era, was Administrator of Northern Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bao, in the Wuding era, was Administrator of Northern Liang.

sentences.zh: 愷弟養，步兵校尉，早卒。

translations.literal: Kai's younger brother Yang was Commandant of the Foot Soldiers and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's younger brother Yang was Commandant of the Foot Soldiers and died young.

sentences.zh: 養弟資，武騎侍郎、河間太守、太僕少卿、汲郡太守。

translations.literal: Yang's younger brother Zi was Gentleman of the Martial Riders, Administrator of Hejian, Junior Director of the Imperial Stud, and Administrator of Ji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yang's younger brother Zi was Gentleman of the Martial Riders, Administrator of Hejian, Junior Director of the Imperial Stud, and Administrator of Ji Commandery.

sentences.zh: 遷龍驤將軍、肆州刺史。

translations.literal: On returning he was appointed General of the Dragon Charger and Inspector of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was appointed General of the Dragon Charger and Inspector of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 還，除武衞將軍，加後將軍。

translations.literal: Again he was appointed General of the Martial Guard and additionally made Rear General.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed General of the Martial Guard and additionally made Rear General.

sentences.zh: 延昌末卒。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yan chang era he died.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yan chang era he died.

sentences.zh: 贈平北將軍、并州刺史，并給帛二百匹，布一百匹，諡曰愍。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Bing Province, and given two hundred bolts of silk and one hundred bolts of cloth; posthumous title Min.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Bing Province, and given two hundred bolts of silk and one hundred bolts of cloth, with the posthumous title Min.

sentences.zh: 子景蠻，[7]莊帝時，撫軍將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His son Jingman, [7] in the time of Emperor Xiaozhuang, was General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Purse.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingman, [7] in the time of Emperor Xiaozhuang, was General Who Pacifies the Army and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Purse.

sentences.zh: 頹弟若周，散騎常侍、尚書。

translations.literal: Tui's younger brother Ruozhou was Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Tui's younger brother Ruozhou was Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太和中，安南將軍、豫州刺史、潁川侯。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was General Who Pacifies the South, Inspector of Yu Province, and Marquis of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he was General Who Pacifies the South, Inspector of Yu Province, and Marquis of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 若周弟壽樂，太和中，北部尚書。

translations.literal: Ruozhou's younger brother Shoule, in the Taihe era, was Director of the Northern Department.
translations.idiomatic: Ruozhou's younger brother Shoule, in the Taihe era, was Director of the Northern Department.

sentences.zh: 安南將軍、懷州刺史，假山陽公，未拜。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the South, Inspector of Huai Province, and Acting Duke of Shanyang—he did not assume the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was General Who Pacifies the South, Inspector of Huai Province, and Acting Duke of Shanyang, but did not assume the appointment.

sentences.zh: 尋除散騎常侍、殿中尚書、晉安侯。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Director of the Palace Secretariat, and Marquis of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Director of the Palace Secretariat, and Marquis of Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈安東將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 頹從叔孤，少以忠直稱。

translations.literal: Tui's younger uncle Gu, from youth, was known for loyalty and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Tui's younger uncle Gu, from youth, was known for loyalty and uprightness.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，以定策功拜車騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne, for his merit in settling the succession he was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne, for his merit in settling the succession he was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 後除鎮軍大將軍、并州刺史、博陵公。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Grand General Who Pacifies the Army, Inspector of Bing Province, and Duke of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Grand General Who Pacifies the Army, Inspector of Bing Province, and Duke of Boling.

sentences.zh: 不治產業，死之日家無餘財，百姓追思之。

translations.literal: He did not manage property; on the day of his death his household had no surplus wealth, and the common people remembered him.
translations.idiomatic: He did not manage property; on the day of his death his household had no surplus wealth, and the common people remembered him fondly.

sentences.zh: 薛野䐗，代人也。

translations.literal: Xueye Zhe was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Xueye Zhe was a native of Dai.

sentences.zh: 父達頭，自姚萇時率部落歸國。

translations.literal: His father Datou, from the time of Yao Chang, led the tribe to submit to the state.
translations.idiomatic: His father Datou, from the time of Yao Chang, led the tribe to submit to the state.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉其忠款，賜爵聊城侯，散員大夫，待以上客之禮，賜妻鄭氏。

translations.literal: Taizu commended his loyal sincerity, granted him the title Marquis of Liaocheng, made him Grand Master of the Scattered Retainers, treated him with the courtesy due a superior guest, and gave him Lady Zheng as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu commended his loyal sincerity, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Liaocheng, made him Grand Master of the Scattered Retainers, treated him with the courtesy due a superior guest, and gave him Lady Zheng in marriage.

sentences.zh: 達頭閑雅恭慎，太祖深器之。

translations.literal: Datou was refined, elegant, respectful, and cautious; Taizu greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Datou was refined, elegant, respectful, and cautious; Taizu greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈平南將軍、冀州刺史，諡曰悼。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Ji Province, with posthumous title Dao.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Ji Province, with the posthumous title Dao.

sentences.zh: 野䐗少失父母，養於宗人利家。

translations.literal: Zhe in youth lost his parents and was raised in the household of his clansman Li.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe in youth lost his parents and was raised in the household of his clansman Li.

sentences.zh: 及長，好學善射。

translations.literal: When he grew up he loved learning and was skilled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he loved learning and was skilled at archery.

sentences.zh: 高宗初，召補羽林。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wencheng's reign he was summoned and appointed to the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Wencheng's reign he was summoned and appointed to the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中，典民籍事，校計戶口，號為稱職。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman Attendant-in-Ordinary, in charge of household registers, and in checking population accounts was called competent.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Gentleman Attendant-in-Ordinary, placed in charge of household registers, and in auditing population accounts was regarded as competent.

sentences.zh: 賜爵順陽子。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Marquis of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 野䐗少孤，父侯不襲，至是錫爵。

translations.literal: Zhe in youth was orphaned; his father's marquisate had not been inherited, and only now was the title granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe in youth was orphaned; his father's marquisate had not been inherited, and only now was the title granted.

sentences.zh: 和平中，除平南將軍、并州刺史，進爵河東公。

translations.literal: In the Heping era he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Bing Province and advanced to Duke of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the Heping era he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Bing Province and advanced to Duke of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 轉太州刺史，在治有聲。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Tai Province; his governance had a good reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Inspector of Tai Province; his governance had a good reputation.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、大將軍、并州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Grand General, and Inspector of Bing Province, with posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Grand General, and Inspector of Bing Province, with the posthumous title Jian.

sentences.zh: 子虎子，姿貌壯偉，明斷有父風。

translations.literal: His son Huzi had a stalwart appearance, was clear and decisive, and had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huzi had a stalwart appearance, was clear and decisive, and had his father's manner.

sentences.zh: 年十三，入侍高宗。

translations.literal: At the age of thirteen he entered attendance on Emperor Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of thirteen he entered attendance on Emperor Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 太安中，遷內行長，典奏諸曹事。

translations.literal: In the Taian era he was transferred to Chief of the Inner Service, in charge of memorials and the affairs of the various bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taian era he was transferred to Chief of the Inner Service, in charge of memorials and the affairs of the various bureaus.

sentences.zh: 當官正直，內外憚之。

translations.literal: Upright in office, inside and outside feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Upright in office, he was feared inside and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 及文明太后臨朝，出虎子為枋頭鎮將。

translations.literal: When the Wenming Empress Dowager assumed the regency, Huzi was sent out as Garrison Commander of Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wenming Empress Dowager assumed the regency, Huzi was sent out as Garrison Commander of Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 虎子素剛簡，為近臣所疾，因小過黜為鎮門士。

translations.literal: Huzi had always been stern and plain; he was envied by those close to the throne and, on a minor fault, was demoted to gate guard at the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Huzi had always been stern and plain; he was envied by those close to the throne and, on a minor fault, was demoted to gate guard at the garrison.

sentences.zh: 及顯祖南巡，次於山陽。

translations.literal: When Xianzu made a southern tour and halted at Shanyang,
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzu made a southern tour and halted at Shanyang,

sentences.zh: 虎子拜訴於路，曰：「臣昔事先帝，過霑重恩。

translations.literal: Huzi bowed and appealed on the road, saying: "Your servant formerly served the late emperor and received his heavy favor.
translations.idiomatic: Huzi bowed and appealed on the road, saying: "Your servant formerly served the late emperor and received his heavy favor.

sentences.zh: 陛下在諒闇之日，臣橫罹非罪，自擯黜此蕃，已經多載，不悟今日得奉聖顏。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty was in the period of mourning, your servant suffered an unjust crime and was cast out to this frontier; many years have passed, and I did not expect today to behold the holy countenance.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty was in the period of mourning, your servant suffered an unjust crime and was cast out to this frontier; many years have passed, and I did not expect today to behold the holy countenance.

sentences.zh: 」遂流涕嗚咽。

translations.literal: " He then wept and sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: " He then wept and sobbed.

sentences.zh: 顯祖曰：「卿先帝舊臣，久屈非所，良用憮然。

translations.literal: Xianzu said: "You are an old minister of the late emperor, long wronged out of your proper place; I am truly grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu said: "You are an old minister of the late emperor, long wronged out of your proper place; I am truly grieved.

sentences.zh: 」詔虎子侍行，訪以政事，數十里中，占對不絕。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered Huzi to attend on the journey and questioned him on government affairs; for several tens of li his answers did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered Huzi to attend on the journey and questioned him on government affairs; for several tens of li his answers did not cease.

sentences.zh: 時山東飢饉，盜賊競起。

translations.literal: At that time the east of the mountains suffered famine, and bandits rose in competition.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the region east of the mountains suffered famine, and bandits rose in competition.

sentences.zh: 相州民孫誨等五百餘人，稱虎子在鎮之日，土境清晏，訴乞虎子。

translations.literal: More than five hundred people of Xiang Province, led by Sun Hui and others, declared that while Huzi was at the garrison the territory within his borders was clear and tranquil, and petitioned that Huzi be sent.
translations.idiomatic: More than five hundred people of Xiang Province, led by Sun Hui and others, declared that while Huzi was at the garrison the territory within his borders was clear and tranquil, and petitioned that Huzi be sent.

sentences.zh: 乃復除枋頭鎮將，即日之任。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Garrison Commander of Fangtou and went to his post that same day.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Garrison Commander of Fangtou and went to his post that same day.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，數州之地，姦徒屏跡。

translations.literal: On reaching the garrison, across several provinces the wicked hid their tracks.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the garrison, across several provinces the wicked hid their tracks.

sentences.zh: 顯祖璽書慰喻。

translations.literal: Xianzu sent an imperial letter of consolation and praise.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu sent an imperial letter of consolation and praise.

sentences.zh: 後除平南將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 顯祖崩，不行。

translations.literal: When Xianzu died he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzu died he did not go.

sentences.zh: 太和二年，襲爵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taihe he inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taihe he inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔虎子督三將出壽春，與劉昶南討。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict ordered Huzi to command three generals out of Shouchun and campaign south with Liu Chang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict ordered Huzi to command three generals out of Shouchun and campaign south with Liu Chang.

sentences.zh: 四年，徐州民桓和等叛逆，屯於五固。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the people of Xu Province, Huan He and others, rebelled and encamped at Wugu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the people of Xu Province, Huan He and others, rebelled and encamped at Wugu.

sentences.zh: 詔虎子為南征都副將，與尉元等討平之。

translations.literal: An edict made Huzi deputy commander-in-chief of the southern expedition; together with Wei Yuan and others he suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Huzi deputy commander-in-chief of the southern expedition; together with Wei Yuan and others he suppressed and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 以本將軍為彭城鎮將。

translations.literal: With his former rank he was made Garrison Commander of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: With his former rank he was made Garrison Commander of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，雅得民和。

translations.literal: On reaching the garrison he naturally won the people's goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the garrison he naturally won the people's goodwill.

sentences.zh: 除開府、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed with an opened headquarters and made Inspector of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed with an opened headquarters and made Inspector of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 時州鎮戍兵，資絹自隨，不入公庫，任其私用，常苦飢寒。

translations.literal: At that time the garrison troops of the province and garrison brought their own silk rations and did not enter the public storehouses; they used them privately as they wished, and constantly suffered hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the provincial and garrison troops brought their own silk rations and did not deposit them in the public storehouses; they used them privately as they wished and constantly suffered hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 虎子上表曰：「臣聞金湯之固，非粟不守；

translations.literal: Huzi submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that metal ramparts and moats cannot be held without grain;
translations.idiomatic: Huzi submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that metal ramparts and moats cannot be held without grain;

sentences.zh: 韓白之勇，非糧不戰。

translations.literal: the bravery of Han Xin and Bai Qi cannot fight without provisions.
translations.idiomatic: the bravery of Han Xin and Bai Qi cannot fight without provisions.

sentences.zh: 故自用兵以來，莫不先積聚，然後圖兼并者也。

translations.literal: Therefore, since troops have been used, none have failed first to accumulate stores and only then to plan conquest.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, since troops have been used, none have failed first to accumulate stores and only then to plan conquest.

sentences.zh: 今江左未賓，鯨鯢待戮，自不委粟彭城，以強豐沛，將何以拓定江關，掃一衡霍？

translations.literal: Now the lands south of the Yangzi are not yet subdued, and great foes await punishment; if we do not entrust grain to Pengcheng to strengthen Feng and Pei, how shall we expand and settle the river passes and sweep clean Heng and Huo?
translations.idiomatic: Now the lands south of the Yangzi are not yet subdued, and great foes await punishment; if we do not entrust grain to Pengcheng to strengthen Feng and Pei, how shall we expand and settle the river passes and sweep clean Heng and Huo?

sentences.zh: 竊惟在鎮之兵，不減數萬，資糧之絹，人十二匹，即自隨身，用度無準，未及代下，不免飢寒。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that the troops in the garrison are no fewer than tens of thousands; each man receives twelve bolts of grain and silk as provisions, which he carries on his person; with no fixed measure of use, before the rotation of garrisons arrives he cannot escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant considers that the troops in the garrison are no fewer than tens of thousands; each man receives twelve bolts of grain and silk as provisions, which he carries on his person; with no fixed measure of use, before the rotation of garrisons arrives he cannot escape hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 論之於公，無毫釐之潤；

translations.literal: Judged for the public, there is not the profit of a hair or a fraction;
translations.idiomatic: Judged for the public, there is not the profit of a hair or a fraction;

sentences.zh: 語其利私，則橫費不足。

translations.literal: spoken of for private advantage, the reckless expenditure is insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: spoken of for private advantage, the reckless expenditure is insufficient.

sentences.zh: 非所謂納民軌度，公私相益也。

translations.literal: This is not what is called bringing the people within the tracks of law so that public and private alike benefit.
translations.idiomatic: This is not what is called bringing the people within the tracks of law so that public and private alike benefit.

sentences.zh: 徐州左右，水陸壤沃，清、汴通流，足盈激灌。

translations.literal: To the left and right of Xu Province the land by water and on land is fertile; the Qing and Bian rivers flow through it, sufficient for irrigation and flooding.
translations.idiomatic: To the left and right of Xu Province the land by water and on land is fertile; the Qing and Bian rivers flow through it, sufficient for irrigation and flooding.

sentences.zh: 其中良田十萬餘頃。

translations.literal: Among them are more than one hundred thousand qing of fine fields.
translations.idiomatic: Among them are more than one hundred thousand qing of fine fields.

sentences.zh: 若以兵絹市牛，分減戍卒，計其牛數，足得萬頭。

translations.literal: If the troops' silk is used to buy oxen and distributed among the garrison soldiers according to their numbers, counting the oxen, there would be fully ten thousand head.
translations.idiomatic: If the troops' silk is used to buy oxen and distributed among the garrison soldiers according to their numbers, counting the oxen, there would be fully ten thousand head.

sentences.zh: 興力公田，必當大獲粟稻。

translations.literal: If public fields are opened with corvée labor, the harvest of grain and rice must be great.
translations.idiomatic: If public fields are opened with corvée labor, the harvest of grain and rice must be great.

sentences.zh: 一歲之中，且給官食，半兵耘植，餘兵尚眾，且耕且守，不妨捍邊。

translations.literal: Within one year the officials' food could be supplied at once; half the troops would till and plant while the remaining troops would still be numerous, farming and guarding together without hindering defense of the border.
translations.idiomatic: Within one year the officials' food could be supplied at once; half the troops would till and plant while the remaining troops would still be numerous, farming and guarding together without hindering defense of the border.

sentences.zh: 一年之收，過於十倍之絹；

translations.literal: The harvest of one year would exceed tenfold the value in silk;
translations.idiomatic: The harvest of one year would exceed tenfold the value in silk;

sentences.zh: 暫時之耕，足充數載之食。

translations.literal: temporary cultivation would fully supply food for several years.
translations.idiomatic: temporary cultivation would fully supply food for several years.

sentences.zh: 於後兵資，唯須內庫，五稔之後，穀帛俱溢。

translations.literal: Afterward the troops' provisions would need only the inner storehouses; within five harvests grain and cloth would both overflow.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the troops' provisions would need only the inner storehouses; within five harvests grain and cloth would both overflow.

sentences.zh: 匪直戍士有豐飽之資，於國有吞敵之勢。

translations.literal: Not only would the garrison soldiers have abundant provisions; the state would also possess the momentum to swallow its foes.
translations.idiomatic: Not only would the garrison soldiers have abundant provisions; the state would also possess the momentum to swallow its foes.

sentences.zh: 昔杜預田宛葉以平吳，充國耕西零以強漢。

translations.literal: Formerly Du Yu farmed Wanye to pacify Wu, and Zhao Chongguo farmed Xiling to strengthen Han.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Du Yu farmed Wanye to pacify Wu, and Zhao Chongguo farmed Xiling to strengthen Han.

sentences.zh: 臣雖識謝古人，任當邊守，庶竭塵露，有增山海。

translations.literal: Your servant's understanding falls short of the ancients, but the charge is on the border; I hope to exhaust the dust of my service and add something to mountain and sea.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's understanding falls short of the ancients, but the charge is on the border; I hope to exhaust the dust of my service and add something to mountain and sea.

sentences.zh: 」高祖納之。

translations.literal: " Gaozu accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu accepted this.

sentences.zh: 又上疏曰：「臣聞先王建不易之軌，萬代承之；

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that the former kings established unchanging tracks, to be inherited for ten thousand generations;
translations.idiomatic: He again submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that the former kings established unchanging tracks, to be inherited for ten thousand generations;

sentences.zh: 聖主垂不刊之制，千載共仰。

translations.literal: sage rulers set down regulations not to be altered, for a thousand generations jointly to look up to them.
translations.idiomatic: sage rulers set down regulations not to be altered, for a thousand generations jointly to look up to them.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下道洽羣生，恩齊造化，仁德所覃，迹超前哲。

translations.literal: Your servant bows to consider that Your Majesty's Way harmonizes all living beings and your grace equals transforming power; the benevolence and virtue you extend surpass the former sages.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant bows to consider that Your Majesty's Way harmonizes all living beings and your grace equals transforming power; the benevolence and virtue you extend surpass the former sages.

sentences.zh: 遠崇古典，留意治方，革前王之弊法，申當今之宜用。

translations.literal: You look far to the ancient canon and attend to methods of governance, reforming the abuses of former kings and applying what is fitting in the present.
translations.idiomatic: You look far to the ancient canon and attend to methods of governance, reforming the abuses of former kings and applying what is fitting in the present.

sentences.zh: 定貢賦之輕重，均品秩之厚薄，庶令百辟足以代耕，編戶享其餘畜。

translations.literal: You fix the lightness or heaviness of tribute and tax and equalize the thickness or thinness of ranks and grades, so that the hundred officials may suffice for substitute farming and registered households may enjoy their surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: You fix the lightness or heaviness of tribute and tax and equalize the thickness or thinness of ranks and grades, so that the hundred officials may suffice for substitute farming and registered households may enjoy their surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 巍乎煥焉，不可量也。

translations.literal: How lofty and radiant— it cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: How lofty and radiant— it cannot be measured.

sentences.zh: 臣竊尋居邊之民，蒙化日淺，戎馬之所，資計素微。

translations.literal: Your servant further considers that the people dwelling on the borders have daily received transforming influence for only a short time; where war horses go, their means of support have always been slight.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant further considers that the people dwelling on the borders have daily received transforming influence for only a short time; where war horses go, their means of support have always been slight.

sentences.zh: 小戶者一丁而已，計其徵調之費，終歲乃有七縑。

translations.literal: A small household has only one adult male; counting the cost of levies and collections, through the year it comes to seven bolts of thin silk.
translations.idiomatic: A small household has only one adult male; counting the cost of levies and collections, through the year it comes to seven bolts of thin silk.

sentences.zh: 去年徵責不備，或有貨易田宅，質妻賣子，呻吟道路，不可忍聞。

translations.literal: Last year collections were not complete, and some sold fields and houses, pawned wives and sold children; their moans along the roads were unbearable to hear.
translations.idiomatic: Last year collections were not complete, and some sold fields and houses, pawned wives and sold children; their moans along the roads were unbearable to hear.

sentences.zh: 今淮南之人，思慕聖化，延頸企足，十室而九。

translations.literal: Now the people of Huainan long for sagely transformation, stretch their necks and stand on tiptoe—nine houses in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Now the people of Huainan long for sagely transformation, stretch their necks and stand on tiptoe—nine houses in ten.

sentences.zh: 恐聞賦重，更懷進退。

translations.literal: I fear that on hearing heavy taxes they will again harbor thoughts of advancing or retreating.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that on hearing heavy taxes they will again harbor thoughts of advancing or retreating.

sentences.zh: 非惟損皇風之盛，慮傷慕義之心。

translations.literal: This is not only to diminish the splendor of imperial civilization; I also worry that it will injure hearts that yearn for righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: This is not only to diminish the splendor of imperial civilization; I also worry that it will injure hearts that yearn for righteousness.

sentences.zh: 且臣所居，與南連接，民情去就，實所諳知。

translations.literal: Moreover, the place where your servant resides adjoins the south on its border; the people's inclinations to come or go are truly what I know well.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the place where your servant resides adjoins the south on its border; the people's inclinations to come or go are truly what I know well.

sentences.zh: 特宜寬省，以招未至。

translations.literal: It is especially fitting to lighten and reduce levies to summon those not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: It is especially fitting to lighten and reduce levies to summon those not yet arrived.

sentences.zh: 其小郡太守，數戶而已。

translations.literal: Their petty commandery administrators number only a few households.
translations.idiomatic: Their petty commandery administrators number only a few households.

sentences.zh: 一請止六尺絹，歲不滿匹。

translations.literal: One request stops at six chi of silk; in a year it does not reach one bolt.
translations.idiomatic: One request stops at six chi of silk; in a year it does not reach one bolt.

sentences.zh: 既委邊捍，取其必死，邀之士重，何吝君輕。

translations.literal: Since they are entrusted with border defense, one takes their certain death; if the weight on the scholar is heavy, why be sparing toward the lord?
translations.idiomatic: Since they are entrusted with border defense, one takes their certain death; if the weight on the scholar is heavy, why be sparing toward the lord?

sentences.zh: 今班制已行，布之天下，不宜忤冒，以亂朝章。

translations.literal: Now the salary system has been put in force and promulgated throughout the realm; it is not fitting to offend against it and thereby disorder the court's regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Now the salary system has been put in force and promulgated throughout the realm; it is not fitting to offend against it and thereby disorder the court's regulations.

sentences.zh: 但猥藉恩私，備位蕃岳，憂責之地，敢不盡言。

translations.literal: But your servant, relying on private favor, holds a post on the frontier border; in a place of anxious responsibility, how dare I not speak fully?
translations.idiomatic: But your servant, relying on private favor, holds a post on the frontier border; in a place of anxious responsibility, how dare I not speak fully?

sentences.zh: 」書奏，文明太皇太后令曰：「俸制已行，不可以小有不平，便虧通式。」

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the Wenming Empress Dowager ordered: "The salary system has already been put in force; one cannot, for a small unevenness here and there, damage the universal regulation."
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, the Wenming Empress Dowager ordered: "The salary system has already been put in force; one cannot, for a small unevenness here and there, damage the universal regulation."

sentences.zh: 在州戍兵，每歲交代，虎子必親自勞送。

translations.literal: For the garrison troops in the province, each year at the rotation of garrisons Huzi always personally saw them off with labor.
translations.idiomatic: For the garrison troops in the province, each year at the rotation of garrisons Huzi always personally saw them off with labor.

sentences.zh: 喪者給其斂帛。

translations.literal: For the dead he supplied burial silk.
translations.idiomatic: For the dead he supplied burial silk.

sentences.zh: 州內遭水，二麥不收，上表請貸民粟，民有車牛者，求詣東兗給之。

translations.literal: Within the province, when water disaster struck and the two wheat harvests failed, he submitted a memorial requesting grain loans to the people; those with carts and oxen were allowed to go to eastern Yan for provision.
translations.idiomatic: Within the province, when water disaster struck and the two wheat harvests failed, he submitted a memorial requesting grain loans to the people; those with carts and oxen were allowed to go to eastern Yan for provision.

sentences.zh: 並如所奏，民得安堵。

translations.literal: All was done as he memorialized, and the people were settled.
translations.idiomatic: All was done as he memorialized, and the people were settled.

sentences.zh: 高祖曾從容問祕書丞李彪曰：「卿頻使江南，徐州刺史政績何如？

translations.literal: Gaozu once casually asked Secretariat Assistant Li Biao: "You have often been envoy to the lands south of the Yangzi—how is the administrative achievement of the Inspector of Xu Province?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu once casually asked Secretariat Assistant Li Biao: "You have often been envoy to the lands south of the Yangzi—how is the administrative achievement of the Inspector of Xu Province?

sentences.zh: 」彪曰：「綏邊布化，甚得其和。

translations.literal: " Biao said: "He soothes the border and spreads civilizing influence; he attains great harmony.
translations.idiomatic: " Biao said: "He soothes the border and spreads civilizing influence; he attains great harmony.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「朕亦知之。
