translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "I know this as well.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu said: "I know this as well.

sentences.zh: 」沛郡太守邵安、下邳太守張攀咸以贓汚，虎子案之於法。

translations.literal: " The Administrators of Pei Commandery Shao An and Xiapi Zhang Pan were both guilty of bribery and corruption; Huzi prosecuted them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: " The Administrators of Pei Commandery Shao An and Xiapi Zhang Pan were both guilty of bribery and corruption; Huzi prosecuted them according to law.

sentences.zh: 安等遣子弟上書，誣虎子南通賊虜。

translations.literal: An and the others sent their younger kinsmen to submit memorials at the capital, falsely accusing Huzi of conniving with southern bandits.
translations.idiomatic: An and the others sent their younger kinsmen to submit memorials at the capital, falsely accusing Huzi of conniving with southern bandits.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「此其妄矣，朕度虎子必不然也。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "This is their wild falsehood; I am sure Huzi is certainly not so.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said: "This is their wild falsehood; I am sure Huzi is certainly not so.

sentences.zh: 」推案果虛。

translations.literal: " Investigation proved it empty.
translations.idiomatic: " Investigation proved it empty.

sentences.zh: 乃下詔曰：「夫君臣體合，則功業可興；

translations.literal: An edict was then issued: "When lord and minister are united in body, achievements can be raised;
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued: "When lord and minister are united in body, achievements can be raised;

sentences.zh: 上下猜懼，則治道替矣。

translations.literal: when above and below suspect and fear each other, the way of governance is replaced.
translations.idiomatic: when above and below suspect and fear each other, the way of governance is replaced.

sentences.zh: 沛郡太守邵安、下邳太守張攀咸以貪惏獲罪，各遣子弟詣闕，告刺史虎子縱民通賊，妄稱無端。

translations.literal: The Administrators of Pei Commandery Shao An and Xiapi Zhang Pan were both punished for greedy cruelty; each sent his sons and younger kinsmen to the palace gates, reporting that Inspector Huzi indulged the people in communicating with bandits and falsely declared groundless charges.
translations.idiomatic: The Administrators of Pei Commandery Shao An and Xiapi Zhang Pan were both punished for greedy cruelty; each sent his sons and younger kinsmen to the palace gates, reporting that Inspector Huzi indulged the people in communicating with bandits and falsely declared groundless charges.

sentences.zh: 安宜賜死，攀及子僧保鞭一百，配敦煌。

translations.literal: An should be ordered to death; Pan and his son Sengbao are to receive one hundred strokes of the whip and be assigned to Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: An should be ordered to death; Pan and his son Sengbao are to receive one hundred strokes of the whip and be assigned to Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 安息他生鞭一百。

translations.literal: An's younger brother Xi is to receive one hundred strokes of the whip in his next life.
translations.idiomatic: An's younger brother Xi is to receive one hundred strokes of the whip in his next life.

sentences.zh: 可集州官兵民等，宣告行決。

translations.literal: The officials, soldiers, and people of the province are to be assembled and the sentence publicly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The officials, soldiers, and people of the province are to be assembled and the sentence publicly carried out.

sentences.zh: 塞彼輕狡之源，開此陳力之效。

translations.literal: Block the source of their frivolous cunning and open this effect of displaying one's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Block the source of their frivolous cunning and open this effect of displaying one's strength.

sentences.zh: 」在州十一載，太和十五年卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: " He was in the province eleven years; in the fifteenth year of Taihe he died at the age of fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: " He was in the province eleven years; in the fifteenth year of Taihe he died at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、鎮南將軍、相州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Guards the South, and Inspector of Xiang Province, with posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General Who Guards the South, and Inspector of Xiang Province, with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 有六子。

translations.literal: He had six sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons.

sentences.zh: 長子世遵，襲爵，例降為侯。

translations.literal: His eldest son Shizun inherited the title and by precedent was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shizun inherited the title and by precedent was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 景明中，為秦州刺史，稍遷左將軍。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era he was Inspector of Qin Province and was gradually promoted to General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingming era he was Inspector of Qin Province and was gradually promoted to General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十二。

translations.literal: He died at the age of forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 長子忱，字安民。

translations.literal: His eldest son Chen, styled Anmin.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Chen, styled Anmin.

sentences.zh: 正光中，襲爵。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era he inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguang era he inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 稍遷鎮南將軍、鉅鹿太守、定州儀同開府諮議參軍、齊獻武王大行臺左丞、中外府司馬。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to General Who Guards the South, Administrator of Julu, Staff Adviser with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies to Prince Xianwu of Qi's Grand Marching Headquarters, and Left Director of the Central and Outer Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to General Who Guards the South, Administrator of Julu, Staff Adviser with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies on Prince Xianwu of Qi's Grand Marching Headquarters, and Left Director of the Central and Outer Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 出為殷州驃騎府長史。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk of the Agile Cavalry Headquarters of Yin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Chief Clerk of the Agile Cavalry Headquarters of Yin Province.

sentences.zh: 武定五年，除鎮北將軍、北廣平太守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wuding he was appointed General Who Guards the North and Administrator of Northern Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wuding he was appointed General Who Guards the North and Administrator of Northern Guangping.

sentences.zh: 為治暴虐，曾因公事，一家之內併殺數人。

translations.literal: His governance was brutal and tyrannical; on one occasion over a public matter he killed several people within a single household.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was brutal and tyrannical; on one occasion over a public matter he killed several people within a single household.

sentences.zh: 為民所訟，將致之罪，遇患，卒於郡。

translations.literal: The people prosecuted him and he was about to be brought to punishment, but he fell ill and died in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The people prosecuted him and he was about to be brought to punishment, but he fell ill and died in the commandery.

sentences.zh: 贈征西將軍、西兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed General Who Campaigns West and Inspector of Western Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed General Who Campaigns West and Inspector of Western Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 忱弟安顥，武定末，東豫州征西府長史。

translations.literal: Chen's younger brother Anhao, at the end of Wuding, was Chief Clerk of the Campaign West Headquarters of Eastern Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's younger brother Anhao, at the end of Wuding, was Chief Clerk of the Campaign West Headquarters of Eastern Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 世遵弟曇慶，少有度量。

translations.literal: Shizun's younger brother Yanqing from youth possessed breadth of mind.
translations.idiomatic: Shizun's younger brother Yanqing from youth possessed breadth of mind.

sentences.zh: 永平中，員外散騎常侍，遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: In the Yongping era he was Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and was transferred to Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongping era he was Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and was transferred to Gentleman of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 年五十一，卒。

translations.literal: At the age of fifty-one he died.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of fifty-one he died.

sentences.zh: 子衍，字元孫，輕財慕義。

translations.literal: His son Yan, styled Yuansun, was light with wealth and admired righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan, styled Yuansun, was light with wealth and admired righteousness.

sentences.zh: 熙平中，為侍御史、奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the Xiping era he was Attending Censor and Court Gentleman for Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiping era he was Attending Censor and Court Gentleman for Attendance.

sentences.zh: 永安中，尚書駕部郎中，行河陰縣事。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era he was Gentleman of the Imperial Stud's Harness Department and acted as magistrate of Heyin County.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yong'an era he was Gentleman of the Imperial Stud's Harness Department and acted as magistrate of Heyin County.

sentences.zh: 卒於正平太守。

translations.literal: He died as Administrator of Zhengping.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Administrator of Zhengping.

sentences.zh: 贈征東將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed General Who Campaigns East and Inspector of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed General Who Campaigns East and Inspector of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 曇慶弟曇寶，初補散騎。

translations.literal: Yanqing's younger brother Yanbao at first was appointed to the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing's younger brother Yanbao at first was appointed to the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔曇寶採遺書於天下。

translations.literal: Gaozu ordered Yanbao to collect lost books throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu ordered Yanbao to collect lost books throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 歷侍御中散、直閤將軍、太子步兵校尉。

translations.literal: He served successively as Attendant of the Imperial Guard and Central Scattered Cavalry, General of the Direct Gate, and Commandant of Foot Soldiers of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Attendant of the Imperial Guard and Central Scattered Cavalry, General of the Direct Gate, and Commandant of Foot Soldiers of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，遣使巡行四方，以曇寶持節、兼散騎常侍、龍驤將軍、南道大使。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xiaowen he was sent as envoy to tour the four quarters; Yanbao was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Acting Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General of the Dragon Charger, and Grand Ambassador of the Southern Route.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was sent as envoy to tour the four quarters; Yanbao was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Acting Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, General of the Dragon Charger, and Grand Ambassador of the Southern Route.

sentences.zh: 曇寶達豫州，卒，年二十九。

translations.literal: When Yanbao reached Yu Province he died at the age of twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanbao reached Yu Province he died at the age of twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 曇寶弟曇尚，有容貌，性寬和。

translations.literal: Yanbao's younger brother Yanshang had a handsome appearance and a mild, harmonious nature.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbao's younger brother Yanshang had a handsome appearance and a mild, harmonious nature.

sentences.zh: 初辟御史，加奉朝請。

translations.literal: At first he was recruited as a censor and made Court Gentleman for Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was recruited as a censor and made Court Gentleman for Attendance.

sentences.zh: 熙平二年，除徐州穀陽戍主，行南陽平郡事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiping he was appointed Garrison Commander of Guyang in Xu Province and acted as magistrate of Nanyangping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xiping he was appointed Garrison Commander of Guyang in Xu Province and acted as magistrate of Nanyangping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office on mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 正光中，詔以陽平隣接蕭衍，綏捍須人，仰尚書舉才而遣。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era an edict said that because Yangping adjoined Xiao Yan, a man was needed to soothe and defend the border; the Imperial Secretariat was ordered to recommend talent and dispatch him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguang era an edict said that because Yangping adjoined Xiao Yan, a man was needed to soothe and defend the border; the Imperial Secretariat was ordered to recommend talent and dispatch him.

sentences.zh: 左僕射蕭寶夤舉曇尚應選，馳驛之郡。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Xiao Baoyin recommended Yanshang as fitting the selection, and he went to the commandery by relay.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Xiao Baoyin recommended Yanshang as fitting the selection, and he went to the commandery by relay.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，徐州刺史元法僧叛入蕭衍，曇尚斬其使人，送首於都督、安樂王鑒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang, when the Inspector of Xu Province Yuan Faseng defected to Xiao Yan, Yanshang beheaded his envoy and sent the head to the Commander-in-Chief, Prince of Anle Jian.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiaochang, when the Inspector of Xu Province Yuan Faseng defected to Xiao Yan, Yanshang beheaded his envoy and sent the head to the Commander-in-Chief, Prince of Anle Jian.

sentences.zh: 鑒不能援，遂為蕭衍將王希聃所陷，拘曇尚送蕭衍。

translations.literal: Jian could not rescue him; he was then trapped by Xiao Yan's general Wang Xichan, who seized Yanshang and sent him to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian could not rescue him; he was then trapped by Xiao Yan's general Wang Xichan, who seized Yanshang and sent him to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 衍以禮遇之，曇尚乞歸，衍乃聽還。

translations.literal: Yan treated him with ceremonial courtesy; Yanshang begged to return, and Yan then permitted him to go back.
translations.idiomatic: Yan treated him with ceremonial courtesy; Yanshang begged to return, and Yan then permitted him to go back.

sentences.zh: 肅宗復其本秩。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong restored his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong restored his former rank.

sentences.zh: 武泰初，尒朱榮擅強并肆，朝廷欲揣其情，除曇尚員外常侍，使於榮，託以慰喻，密以觀之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wutai, when Erzhu Rong seized power in Bing and Si, the court wished to gauge his intentions and appointed Yanshang Extraordinary Regular Attendant, sending him to Rong under the pretext of consolation while secretly observing him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wutai, when Erzhu Rong seized power in Bing and Si, the court wished to gauge his intentions and appointed Yanshang Extraordinary Regular Attendant, sending him to Rong under the pretext of consolation while secretly observing him.

sentences.zh: 建義初，除司徒左長史、兼吏部尚書，授太原王尒朱榮官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was appointed Left Chief of the Ministry of Rites and Acting Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and invested Prince of Taiyuan Erzhu Rong with office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi he was appointed Left Chief of the Ministry of Rites and Acting Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and invested Prince of Taiyuan Erzhu Rong with office.

sentences.zh: 還，賜爵永安侯。

translations.literal: On returning he was granted the title Marquis of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was granted the title Marquis of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 尋除後將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Rear General and Inspector of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed Rear General and Inspector of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮之死，授持節、兼尚書北道行臺，代魏蘭根。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died he was given the Staff of Authority and made Acting Director of the Imperial Secretariat on the Northern Route, replacing Wei Langen.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong died he was given the Staff of Authority and made Acting Director of the Imperial Secretariat on the Northern Route, replacing Wei Langen.

sentences.zh: 後為鎮東將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was made General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Purse.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Purse.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，加征東將軍，行兗州事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was additionally made General Who Campaigns East and acted as magistrate of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taichang he was additionally made General Who Campaigns East and acted as magistrate of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 天平中，除驃騎大將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he was appointed Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianping era he was appointed Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 曇尚凡歷三州，俱稱貪虐。

translations.literal: Yanshang in all held three provinces and in each was called greedy and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang in all held three provinces and in each was called greedy and cruel.

sentences.zh: 還，除將作大匠，卒於官，年六十一。

translations.literal: On returning he was appointed Director of Palace Construction and died in office at the age of sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was appointed Director of Palace Construction and died in office at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈都督瀛滄二州諸軍事、本將軍、儀同三司、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Ying and Cang provinces, to his former generalship, with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Ying and Cang provinces, confirmed in his former generalship, with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 子仲芬，武定中，齊文襄王中外府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: His son Zhongfen, in the Wuding era, was Military Registrar of Prince Wenxiang of Qi's Central and Outer Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongfen, in the Wuding era, was Military Registrar of Prince Wenxiang of Qi's Central and Outer Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 曇尚弟琡，字曇珍。

translations.literal: Yanshang's younger brother Zhu, styled Yanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang's younger brother Zhu, styled Yanzhen.

sentences.zh: 武定末，儀同三司、尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he held the same privileges as the Three Excellencies and was Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he held ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies and was Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 宇文福，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Yuwen Fu was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Fu was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 其先南單于之遠屬，世為擁部大人。

translations.literal: His ancestors were distant kin of the Southern Chanyu; for generations they were chiefs of the Yong tribe.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were distant kin of the Southern Chanyu; for generations they were chiefs of the Yong tribe.

sentences.zh: 祖活撥，仕慕容垂，為唐郡內史、遼東公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Huobo served Murong Chui as Internal Secretary of Tang Commandery and Duke of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Huobo served Murong Chui as Internal Secretary of Tang Commandery and Duke of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 太祖之平慕容寶，活撥入國，為第一客。

translations.literal: When Taizu pacified Murong Bao, Huobo entered the state and became the foremost guest.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu pacified Murong Bao, Huobo entered the state and became the foremost guest.

sentences.zh: 福少驍果，有膂力。

translations.literal: Fu from youth was fierce and resolute and possessed strength.
translations.idiomatic: Fu from youth was fierce and resolute and possessed strength.

sentences.zh: 太和初，拜羽林郎將，遷建節將軍，賜爵新昌侯、南征都將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was appointed Captain of the Feathered Forest, transferred to General Who Establishes Discipline, granted the title Marquis of Xinchang, and made Commander-in-Chief of the Southern Expedition.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taihe he was appointed Captain of the Feathered Forest, transferred to General Who Establishes Discipline, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xinchang, and made Commander-in-Chief of the Southern Expedition.

sentences.zh: 擊蕭賾有功，授顯武將軍。

translations.literal: He attacked Xiao Ze with merit and was appointed General Who Displays Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Xiao Ze with merit and was appointed General Who Displays Martiality.

sentences.zh: 尋除恢武將軍、北征都將，特賜戎服。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed General Who Restores Martiality and Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Expedition, and was specially granted military dress.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed General Who Restores Martiality and Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Expedition, and was specially granted military dress.

sentences.zh: 破蠕蠕別部，獲萬餘。

translations.literal: He defeated a separate division of the Rouran and captured more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated a separate division of the Rouran and captured more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 還，除都牧給事。

translations.literal: On returning he was appointed Attendant of the Imperial Herd.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was appointed Attendant of the Imperial Herd.

sentences.zh: 十七年，車駕南討，假冠軍將軍、後軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the imperial procession made a southern campaign; he was acting General Who Overcomes the Enemy and Rear General.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the imperial procession made a southern campaign; he was acting General Who Overcomes the Enemy and Rear General.

sentences.zh: 時仍遷洛，敕福檢行牧馬之所。

translations.literal: At that time the capital was moved to Luo; an edict ordered Fu to inspect places for pasturing horses.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the capital was moved to Luo; an edict ordered Fu to inspect places for pasturing horses.

sentences.zh: 福規石濟以西、河內以東，拒黃河南北千里為牧地。

translations.literal: Fu marked off west of Shiji and east of Henei, from the Yellow River north and south for a thousand li, as pasture land.
translations.idiomatic: Fu marked off west of Shiji and east of Henei, from the Yellow River north and south for a thousand li, as pasture land.

sentences.zh: 事尋施行，今之馬場是也。

translations.literal: The matter was soon put into effect; today's horse pastures are this.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was soon put into effect; today's horse pastures are this.

sentences.zh: 及從代移雜畜於牧所，福善於將養，並無損耗，高祖嘉之。

translations.literal: When miscellaneous livestock were moved from Dai to the pastures, Fu was skilled at tending them and none were lost or damaged; Gaozu commended him.
translations.idiomatic: When miscellaneous livestock were moved from Dai to the pastures, Fu was skilled at tending them and none were lost or damaged; Gaozu commended him.

sentences.zh: 尋補司衞監。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Supervisor of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed Supervisor of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 從駕豫州，加冠軍將軍、西道都將、假節、征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial procession to Yu Province and was made General Who Overcomes the Enemy, Commander-in-Chief of the Western Route, Acting Bearer of the Staff of Authority, and General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the imperial procession to Yu Province and was made General Who Overcomes the Enemy, Commander-in-Chief of the Western Route, Acting Bearer of the Staff of Authority, and General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 領精騎一千，專殿駕後。

translations.literal: He led a thousand picked cavalry and alone guarded the rear of the procession.
translations.idiomatic: He led a thousand picked cavalry and alone guarded the rear of the procession.

sentences.zh: 未幾，轉驍騎將軍，仍領太僕、典牧令。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to General of Agile Cavalry and still headed the Imperial Stud and Director of Pasturage.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to General of Agile Cavalry and still headed the Imperial Stud and Director of Pasturage.

sentences.zh: 從駕征南陽，兼武衞將軍。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial procession in the campaign against Nanyang and was additionally made General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the imperial procession in the campaign against Nanyang and was additionally made General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，車駕南討，遣福與右衞將軍楊播為前軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year the imperial procession made a southern campaign and sent Fu together with General of the Right Guard Yang Bo as the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year the imperial procession made a southern campaign and sent Fu together with General of the Right Guard Yang Bo as the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 至鄧城，福選兵簡將，為攻圍之勢。

translations.literal: On reaching Dengcheng, Fu selected troops and generals and formed the momentum of siege and encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Dengcheng, Fu selected troops and generals and formed the momentum of siege and encirclement.

sentences.zh: 高祖望福軍法齊整，將士閑習，大被褒歎。

translations.literal: Gaozu looked on Fu's army as orderly in its regulations and its officers and soldiers practiced and skilled, and greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu looked on Fu's army as orderly in its regulations and its officers and soldiers practiced and skilled, and greatly praised him.

sentences.zh: 蕭鸞遣其尚書崔慧景、黃門郎蕭衍率眾十萬來救。

translations.literal: Xiao Luan sent his Director of the Imperial Secretariat Cui Huijing and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Xiao Yan at the head of a host of one hundred thousand to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Luan sent his Director of the Imperial Secretariat Cui Huijing and Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Xiao Yan at the head of a host of one hundred thousand to rescue.

sentences.zh: 高祖指麾將士，敕福領高車羽林五百騎出賊南面，奪其橋道，遏絕歸路。

translations.literal: Gaozu directed the officers and soldiers and ordered Fu to lead five hundred picked cavalry of the Gaoche Feathered Guard out on the enemy's southern flank, seize their bridges and roads, and cut off their route of return.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu directed the officers and soldiers and ordered Fu to lead five hundred picked cavalry of the Gaoche Feathered Guard out on the enemy's southern flank, seize their bridges and roads, and cut off their route of return.

sentences.zh: 賊眾大恐，六道來戰。

translations.literal: The enemy host was greatly afraid and came to battle from six directions.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy host was greatly afraid and came to battle from six directions.

sentences.zh: 福據鞍誓眾，身先士卒，賊不得前，遂大奔潰。

translations.literal: Fu leaned on his saddle and swore to the host, taking the lead among the soldiers; the bandits could not advance and then fled in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Fu leaned on his saddle and swore to the host, taking the lead among the soldiers; the bandits could not advance and then fled in great rout.

sentences.zh: 賜爵昌黎伯，正武衞，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Earl of Changli, made Regular Martial Guard, and additionally General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Earl of Changli, made Regular Martial Guard, and additionally General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 尋以高車叛，命加征北將軍、北征都將，追討之。

translations.literal: Soon after, because the Gaoche rebelled, he was ordered as Acting General Who Campaigns North and Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Expedition to pursue and attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, because the Gaoche rebelled, he was ordered as Acting General Who Campaigns North and Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Expedition to pursue and attack them.

sentences.zh: 軍敗被黜。

translations.literal: The army was defeated and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The army was defeated and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 景明初，乃起拜平遠將軍、南征統軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingming era he was then raised and appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and Commander-in-Chief of the Southern Expedition.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingming era he was then raised and appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and Commander-in-Chief of the Southern Expedition.

sentences.zh: 進計於都督彭城王勰曰：「建安是淮南重鎮，彼此要衝。

translations.literal: He advanced a plan to the Commander-in-Chief, Prince of Pengcheng Xie, saying: "Jian'an is a strategic stronghold of Huainan and a vital point for both sides.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced a plan to the Commander-in-Chief, Prince of Pengcheng Xie, saying: "Jian'an is a strategic stronghold of Huainan and a vital point for both sides.

sentences.zh: 得之則義陽易圖，不獲則壽春難保。

translations.literal: If we obtain it, Yiyang will be easy to take; if we do not obtain it, Shouchun will be hard to hold.
translations.idiomatic: If we obtain it, Yiyang will be easy to take; if we do not obtain it, Shouchun will be hard to hold.

sentences.zh: 」勰然之。

translations.literal: " Xie approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Xie approved.

sentences.zh: 及勰為州，遂令福攻建安。

translations.literal: When Xie became inspector of the province, he then ordered Fu to attack Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie became inspector of the province, he then ordered Fu to attack Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 建安降，以勳封襄樂縣開國男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: Jian'an surrendered; for merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Xiangle with an estate of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Jian'an surrendered; for merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Xiangle with an estate of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 除太僕少卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed Junior Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Junior Director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 尋以衍將寇邊，假節、征虜將軍，領兵出三關討之。

translations.literal: Soon after, because Yan's generals raided the border, he was given the Staff of Authority, made General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians, and led troops out through the Three Passes to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, because Yan's generals raided the border, he was given the Staff of Authority, made General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians, and led troops out through the Three Passes to attack them.

sentences.zh: 又詔福行豫州事，與東豫州刺史田益宗共相影援，綏遏蠻楚。

translations.literal: Again an edict ordered Fu to act as magistrate of Yu Province; together with the Inspector of Eastern Yu Province Tian Yizong he mutually supported each other, soothing and restraining the Man of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Again an edict ordered Fu to act as magistrate of Yu Province; together with the Inspector of Eastern Yu Province Tian Yizong he mutually supported each other, soothing and restraining the Man of Chu.

sentences.zh: 還，為光祿大夫，轉太僕卿。

translations.literal: On returning he was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and transferred to Grand Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and transferred to Grand Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，以本官領左衞將軍，除散騎常侍、都官尚書，加安東將軍、營州大中正。

translations.literal: In the Yan chang era, with his former office he headed the Left Guard, was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Director of the Ministry of Justice, and additionally made General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Rectifier of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yan chang era, with his former office he headed the Left Guard, was appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Director of the Ministry of Justice, and additionally made General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Rectifier of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，除鎮北將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping he was appointed General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiping he was appointed General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 福性忠清，在公嚴毅，以信御民，甚得聲譽。

translations.literal: Fu was loyal and clear by nature; in public office he was stern and resolute; he governed the people by trust and had a very good reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was loyal and clear by nature; in public office he was stern and resolute; he governed the people by trust and had a very good reputation.

sentences.zh: 解任，復除太僕卿。

translations.literal: On leaving his post he was again appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving his post he was again appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 又為金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Again he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Purse.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Purse.

sentences.zh: 出除散騎常侍，都督懷朔、沃野、武川三鎮諸軍事，征北將軍，懷朔鎮將。

translations.literal: He went out as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of the three garrisons of Huaishuo, Woye, and Wuchuan, General Who Campaigns North, and Garrison Commander of Huaishuo.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of the three garrisons of Huaishuo, Woye, and Wuchuan, General Who Campaigns North, and Garrison Commander of Huaishuo.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，遇病卒。

translations.literal: On reaching the garrison he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the garrison he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 詔遣主書樂安嘉赴弔。

translations.literal: An edict sent the Master of Documents Le'an Jia to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent the Master of Documents Le'an Jia to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 贈車騎大將軍、定州刺史，開國如故，諡曰貞惠。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Ding Province; his state enfeoffment remained as before; posthumous title Zhenhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Ding Province; his state enfeoffment remained as before, with the posthumous title Zhenhui.

sentences.zh: 長子善，字慶孫，襲爵。

translations.literal: His eldest son Shan, styled Qingsun, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shan, styled Qingsun, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 自司空掾，稍遷平南將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: From staff member of the Ministry of Works he was gradually promoted to General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: From staff member of the Ministry of Works he was gradually promoted to General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 孝昌末，北征戰歿。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiaochang he died in battle on the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Xiaochang he died in battle on the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 贈車騎將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 善弟延，字慶壽，體貌魁岸，眉目疎朗。

translations.literal: Shan's younger brother Yan, styled Qingshou, had a stalwart physique and sparse, clear features.
translations.idiomatic: Shan's younger brother Yan, styled Qingshou, had a stalwart physique and sparse, clear features.

sentences.zh: 永平中，釋褐奉朝請，直後、員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the Yongping era he left the purple as Court Gentleman for Attendance, Rear Attendant, and Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongping era he left the purple as Court Gentleman for Attendance, Rear Attendant, and Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 以父老，詔聽隨侍在瀛州。

translations.literal: Because his father was old, an edict permitted him to follow and attend him in Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father was old, an edict permitted him to follow and attend him in Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 屬大乘妖黨突入州城，延率奴客戰，死者數人，身被重創，賊乃小退，而縱火燒齋閣。

translations.literal: When the Mahayana cult bandits burst into the provincial city, Yan led retainers and clients to fight; several of his men died and he himself received heavy wounds, so the bandits retreated slightly but then set fire and burned the chapel pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mahayana cult bandits burst into the provincial city, Yan led retainers and clients to fight; several of his men died and he himself received heavy wounds, so the bandits retreated slightly but then set fire and burned the chapel pavilion.

sentences.zh: 福時在內，延突火而入，抱福出外，支體灼爛，髮盡為燼。

translations.literal: Fu was then inside; Yan dashed through the fire to enter, carried Fu outside, and his limbs were burned and mangled until his hair was entirely ash.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was then inside; Yan dashed through the fire to enter, carried Fu outside, and his limbs were burned and mangled until his hair was entirely ash.

sentences.zh: 於是勒眾與賊苦戰，賊乃散走。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drove the host and fought bitterly with the bandits, and the bandits then scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he drove the host and fought bitterly with the bandits, and the bandits then scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 以此見稱。

translations.literal: For this he won praise.
translations.idiomatic: For this he won praise.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，授假節、建威將軍、西道別將，赴援關隴，有戰功。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era he was appointed Acting Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Establishes Might, and Separate Commander of the Western Route; he went to rescue Guan and Long with battle achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era he was appointed Acting Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Establishes Might, and Separate Commander of the Western Route; he went to rescue Guan and Long with battle achievements.

sentences.zh: 除員外散騎常侍，轉直寢。

translations.literal: He was appointed Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and transferred to Direct Attendant of the Inner Apartments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and transferred to Direct Attendant of the Inner Apartments.

sentences.zh: 與万俟醜奴戰沒。

translations.literal: He died in battle with Moqi Chounu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in battle with Moqi Chounu.

sentences.zh: 贈冠軍將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed General Who Overcomes the Enemy and Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed General Who Overcomes the Enemy and Inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 子仲鸞，武定末，齊王丞相府長流參軍。

translations.literal: His son Zhongluan, at the end of Wuding, was Senior Flow Registrar of the Prince of Qi's Chancellor's Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongluan, at the end of Wuding, was Senior Flow Registrar of the Prince of Qi's Chancellor's Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 慶壽弟慶安，歷給事中、尚書殿中郎中。

translations.literal: Qingshou's younger brother Qing'an served successively as Gentleman Attendant-in-Ordinary and Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat's Hall Department.
translations.idiomatic: Qingshou's younger brother Qing'an served successively as Gentleman Attendant-in-Ordinary and Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat's Hall Department.

sentences.zh: 後加平北將軍、武衞將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was additionally made General Who Pacifies the North and General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was additionally made General Who Pacifies the North and General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 河陰遇害，贈征東將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He met disaster at Heyin; posthumously appointed General Who Campaigns East and Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He met disaster at Heyin; he was posthumously appointed General Who Campaigns East and Inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 長子仲融。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zhongrong.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zhongrong.

sentences.zh: 融弟仲衍。

translations.literal: Rong's younger brother Zhongyan.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's younger brother Zhongyan.

sentences.zh: 費于，代人也。

translations.literal: Fei Yu was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Yu was a native of Dai.

sentences.zh: 袓峻，仕赫連昌，為寧東將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jun served Helian Chang as General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jun served Helian Chang as General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 泰常末，率眾來降，拜龍驤將軍，賜爵犍為公。

translations.literal: At the end of the Taichang era he led his host to surrender and was appointed General of the Dragon Charger and granted the title Duke of Qianwei.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Taichang era he led his host to surrender and was appointed General of the Dragon Charger and enfeoffed as Duke of Qianwei.

sentences.zh: 後遷征南將軍、廣阿鎮大將，徙爵下邳公。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to General Who Campaigns South and Grand Garrison Commander of Guang'a, and his title was moved to Duke of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to General Who Campaigns South and Grand Garrison Commander of Guang'a, and his title was moved to Duke of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 父郁，以隨父歸誠勳，賜五等男，除燕郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Yu, for the merit of following his father in returning in loyalty, was granted the fifth-rank rank of baron and appointed Administrator of Yan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu, for the merit of following his father in returning in loyalty, was granted the fifth rank of baron and appointed Administrator of Yan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈幽州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed Inspector of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Inspector of You Province.

sentences.zh: 于少有節操，起家內三郎。

translations.literal: Yu from youth possessed integrity of conduct and began his career as an Inner Third-Rank Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yu from youth possessed integrity of conduct and began his career as an Inner Third-Rank Attendant.

sentences.zh: 世祖南伐，從駕至江。

translations.literal: When Shizu campaigned south he followed the imperial procession to the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu campaigned south he followed the imperial procession to the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 以宿衞之勤，除寧遠將軍，賜爵松楊男。

translations.literal: For diligence in palace guard service he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and granted the title Baron of Songyang.
translations.idiomatic: For diligence in palace guard service he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and enfeoffed as Baron of Songyang.

sentences.zh: 遷商賈部二曹令，除平南將軍、懷州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief of the Second Bureau of the Merchants Department and appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Huai Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chief of the Second Bureau of the Merchants Department and appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Huai Province.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子萬，襲。

translations.literal: His son Wan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 太和初，除平南將軍、梁國鎮將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Garrison Commander of Liang State.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taihe he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Garrison Commander of Liang State.

sentences.zh: 後高祖南伐，萬從駕渡淮，戰歿。

translations.literal: Later, when Gaozu campaigned south, Wan followed the imperial procession across the Huai and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Gaozu campaigned south, Wan followed the imperial procession across the Huai and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮東將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed General Who Guards the East and Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed General Who Guards the East and Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 子穆，字朗興。

translations.literal: His son Mu, styled Langxing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mu, styled Langxing.

sentences.zh: 性剛烈，有壯氣，頗涉書史，好尚功名。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern and fierce, possessed bold spirit, was fairly versed in books and histories, and loved to pursue fame and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was stern and fierce, possessed bold spirit, was fairly versed in books and histories, and loved to pursue fame and achievement.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，襲男爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he inherited the baron's title.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he inherited the baron's title.

sentences.zh: 後除夏州別駕，尋加寧遠將軍，轉涇州平西府長史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Vice-Prefect of Xia Province; soon after he was additionally made General Who Pacifies the Distance and transferred to Chief Clerk of the Pacify-West Headquarters in Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Vice-Prefect of Xia Province; soon after he was additionally made General Who Pacifies the Distance and transferred to Chief Clerk of the Pacify-West Headquarters in Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 時刺史皇甫集，靈太后之元舅，恃外戚之親，多為非法。

translations.literal: At that time the Inspector Huangfu Ji was the Empress Dowager's eldest uncle by the maternal line and, relying on his connection as maternal kin, did many unlawful things.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Inspector Huangfu Ji was the Empress Dowager's eldest uncle by the maternal line and, relying on his connection as maternal kin, did many unlawful things.

sentences.zh: 穆正色匡諫，集亦憚之。

translations.literal: Mu with stern countenance corrected and remonstrated, and Ji also feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Mu with stern countenance corrected and remonstrated, and Ji also feared him.

sentences.zh: 轉安定太守，仍為長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Anding and still served as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Administrator of Anding and still served as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 還朝，拜左軍將軍，轉河陰令，有嚴明之稱。

translations.literal: On returning to court he was appointed General of the Left Army and transferred to Magistrate of Heyin, with a reputation for stern clarity.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was appointed General of the Left Army and transferred to Magistrate of Heyin, with a reputation for stern clarity.

sentences.zh: 時蠕蠕主婆羅門自涼州歸降，其部眾因飢侵掠邊邑，詔穆銜命宣慰，便皆款附。

translations.literal: At that time the Rouran ruler Poluomen returned in submission from Liang Province; his tribesmen, because of famine, raided and plundered the border settlements; an edict ordered Mu to bear credentials and proclaim consolation, and they all at once submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Rouran ruler Poluomen returned in submission from Liang Province; his tribesmen, because of famine, raided and plundered the border settlements; an edict ordered Mu to bear credentials and proclaim consolation, and they all at once submitted.

sentences.zh: 明年復叛，入寇涼州。

translations.literal: The next year they rebelled again and invaded Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they rebelled again and invaded Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 除穆輔國將軍、假征虜將軍、兼尚書左丞、西北道行臺，仍為別將，往討之。

translations.literal: Mu was appointed General Who Assists the State, Acting General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians, Acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Commissioner of the Northwestern Route, and still served as separate commander to go and attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Mu was appointed General Who Assists the State, Acting General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians, Acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and Commissioner of the Northwestern Route, and still served as separate commander to go and attack them.

sentences.zh: 穆至涼州，蠕蠕遁走。

translations.literal: When Mu reached Liang Province the Rouran fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu reached Liang Province the Rouran fled.

sentences.zh: 穆謂其所部曰：「夷狄獸心，唯利是視，見敵便走，乘虛復出。

translations.literal: Mu said to his subordinates: "The barbarians have the hearts of beasts; they look only to profit, flee on seeing the enemy, and burst out again when they find an opening.
translations.idiomatic: Mu said to his subordinates: "The barbarians have the hearts of beasts; they look only to profit, flee on seeing the enemy, and burst out again when they find an opening.

sentences.zh: 今王師來討，雖畏威逃跡，然軍還之後，必來侵暴。

translations.literal: Now the royal army has come to punish them; though they fear our might and flee, after the army returns they are sure to come raiding and ravaging.
translations.idiomatic: Now the royal army has come to punish them; though they fear our might and flee, after the army returns they are sure to come raiding and ravaging.

sentences.zh: 今欲羸師誘致，冀獲一戰，若不令其破膽，終恐疲於奔命。

translations.literal: Now I wish to lead a weakened army to lure them in, hoping to obtain one battle; if we do not break their courage, in the end we shall be worn out by constant pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to lead a weakened army to lure them in, hoping to obtain one battle; if we do not break their courage, in the end we shall be worn out by constant pursuit.

sentences.zh: 」眾咸然之。

translations.literal: " The host all approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The host all approved.

sentences.zh: 穆乃簡練精騎，伏於山谷，使羸步之眾為外營以誘之。

translations.literal: Mu then picked and trained picked cavalry and hid them in a valley, while weak foot soldiers were made an outer camp to lure them.
translations.idiomatic: Mu then picked and trained elite cavalry and hid them in a valley, while weak foot soldiers were made an outer camp to lure them.

sentences.zh: 賊騎覘見，謂為信弱，俄而競至。

translations.literal: The enemy cavalry observed and considered them truly weak; presently they raced to the spot.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy cavalry observed and considered them truly weak; presently they raced to the spot.

sentences.zh: 穆伏兵奔擊，大破之，斬其帥郁厥烏爾、俟斤十代等，獲生口雜畜甚眾。

translations.literal: Mu's hidden troops charged out and struck; they were greatly defeated, beheading their commanders Yujue Wu'er, Houjin Shidai, and others, and capturing many living captives and mixed livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Mu's hidden troops charged out and struck; they were greatly defeated, beheading their commanders Yujue Wu'er, Houjin Shidai, and others, and capturing many living captives and mixed livestock.

sentences.zh: 及六鎮反叛，詔穆為別將，隸都督李崇北伐。

translations.literal: When the Six Garrisons rebelled, an edict made Mu a separate commander subordinate to the Commander-in-Chief Li Chong on the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Garrisons rebelled, an edict made Mu a separate commander subordinate to the Commander-in-Chief Li Chong on the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 都督崔暹失利，崇將班師，會諸將議曰：「朔州是白道之衝，賊之咽喉，若此處不全，則并肆危矣。

translations.literal: The Commander-in-Chief Cui Kuang suffered defeat; when Chong was about to withdraw the army, he met with the generals in council and said: "Shuo Province is the vital pass of the White Road and the throat of the bandits; if this place is not secured, then Bing and Si will be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: The Commander-in-Chief Cui Kuang suffered defeat; when Chong was about to withdraw the army, he met with the generals in council and said: "Shuo Province is the vital pass of the White Road and the throat of the bandits; if this place is not secured, then Bing and Si will be in peril.

sentences.zh: 今欲選諸將一人，留以鎮捍。

translations.literal: Now I wish to choose one of the generals to remain and garrison and defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to choose one of the generals to remain and garrison and defend it.

sentences.zh: 不知誰堪此任？

translations.literal: Who is fit for this charge?
translations.idiomatic: Who is fit for this charge?

sentences.zh: 」僉曰：「無過穆者。

translations.literal: " All said: "None surpasses Mu."
translations.idiomatic: " All said: "None surpasses Mu."

sentences.zh: 」崇乃請為朔州刺史，仍本將軍，尋改除雲州刺史。

translations.literal: Chong then requested to be made Inspector of Shuo Province, still with his former generalship, and soon after was transferred to Inspector of Yun Province.
translations.idiomatic: Chong then requested that Mu be made Inspector of Shuo Province, still with his former generalship, and soon after he was transferred to Inspector of Yun Province.

sentences.zh: 穆招離聚散，頗得人心。

translations.literal: Mu gathered those who had scattered and won considerable hearts among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Mu gathered those who had scattered and won considerable hearts among the people.

sentences.zh: 時北境州鎮，悉皆淪沒，唯穆獨據一城，四面抗拒。

translations.literal: At that time the northern border provinces and garrisons all fell; only Mu alone held one city and resisted on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the northern border provinces and garrisons all fell; only Mu alone held one city and resisted on four sides.

sentences.zh: 久之，援軍不至，兼行路阻塞，糧仗俱盡。

translations.literal: After a long time relief armies did not arrive; moreover the routes were blocked and grain and weapons were all exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time relief armies did not arrive; moreover the routes were blocked and grain and weapons were all exhausted.

sentences.zh: 穆知勢窮，乃棄城南走，投尒朱榮於秀容。

translations.literal: Mu knew the situation was hopeless and therefore abandoned the city and fled south, throwing himself on Erzhu Rong at Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: Mu knew the situation was hopeless and therefore abandoned the city and fled south, throwing himself on Erzhu Rong at Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 既而詣闕請罪，詔原之。

translations.literal: Afterward he went to the palace to request punishment and was pardoned by edict.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he went to the palace to request punishment and was pardoned by edict.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，二絳蜀反，以穆為都督，討平之。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era the two Jiang and Shu of Jiang rebelled; Mu was made Commander-in-Chief and suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era the two Jiang and Shu of Jiang rebelled; Mu was made Commander-in-Chief and suppressed and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 拜前將軍、散騎常侍，遷平南將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Forward General and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and transferred to General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Forward General and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and transferred to General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 妖賊李洪於陽城起逆，連結蠻左，詔穆兼武衞將軍，率眾討擊，破於關口之南。

translations.literal: The sorcerer-rebel Li Hong rose in Yangcheng and linked with Man of the left; an edict made Mu additionally General of the Martial Guard and ordered him to lead troops to attack; he defeated them south of the Pass mouth.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerer-rebel Li Hong rose in Yangcheng and linked with Man of the left; an edict made Mu additionally General of the Martial Guard and ordered him to lead troops to attack; he defeated them south of the Pass mouth.

sentences.zh: 遷金紫光祿大夫，正武衞將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Purse and Regular Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Purse and Regular Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮向洛，靈太后徵穆，令屯小平。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong advanced on Luo, Empress Dowager Ling summoned Mu and ordered him to encamp at Xiaoping.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong advanced on Luo, Empress Dowager Ling summoned Mu and ordered him to encamp at Xiaoping.

sentences.zh: 及榮推奉莊帝，河梁不守，穆遂棄眾先降。

translations.literal: When Rong raised Emperor Xiaozhuang and the Heyin crossing could not be held, Mu then abandoned his troops and surrendered first.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong raised Emperor Xiaozhuang and the Heyin crossing could not be held, Mu then abandoned his troops and surrendered first.

sentences.zh: 穆素為榮所知，見之甚悅。

translations.literal: Mu had long been known to Rong, and on seeing him Rong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Mu had long been known to Rong, and on seeing him Rong was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 穆潛說榮曰：「公士馬不出萬人，今長驅向洛，前無橫陳者，正以推奉主上，順民心故耳。

translations.literal: Mu secretly urged Rong, saying: "Your lordship's men and horses do not exceed ten thousand; now you drive straight to Luo and there is no blocking army before you only because you are raising the sovereign above and following the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Mu secretly urged Rong, saying: "Your lordship's men and horses do not exceed ten thousand; now you drive straight to Luo and there is no blocking army before you only because you are raising the sovereign above and following the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 既無戰勝之威，羣情素不厭伏。

translations.literal: Yet you have no aura of victorious might, and the multitude by nature has never been content to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you have no aura of victorious might, and the multitude by nature has never been content to submit.

sentences.zh: 今以京師之眾，百官之盛，一知公之虛實，必有輕侮之心。

translations.literal: Now with the host of the capital and the splendor of the hundred officials, once they know your lordship's emptiness and fullness they are sure to harbor a heart of contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Now with the host of the capital and the splendor of the hundred officials, once they know your lordship's emptiness and fullness they are sure to harbor a heart of contempt.

sentences.zh: 若不大行誅罰，更樹親黨，公還北之日，恐不得度太行而內難作矣。

translations.literal: If you do not carry out great executions and punishments and plant new partisans, on the day your lordship returns north I fear you will not cross the Taihang before internal trouble arises.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not carry out great executions and punishments and plant new partisans, on the day your lordship returns north I fear you will not cross the Taihang before internal trouble arises.

sentences.zh: 」榮心然之。

translations.literal: " Rong was persuaded in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: " Rong was persuaded in his heart.

sentences.zh: 於是遂有河陰之事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the affair at Heyin came about.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the affair at Heyin came about.

sentences.zh: 天下聞之，莫不切齒。

translations.literal: When the realm heard of it, none did not gnash their teeth.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm heard of it, none did not gnash their teeth.

sentences.zh: 榮入洛，穆遷中軍將軍、吏部尚書，魯縣開國侯，食邑八百戶，又領夏州大中正。

translations.literal: When Rong entered Luo, Mu was transferred to General of the Central Army and Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Marquis of Lu County with an estate of eight hundred households, and additionally headed the Grand Rectifier of Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong entered Luo, Mu was transferred to General of the Central Army and Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Marquis of Lu County with an estate of eight hundred households, and additionally headed the Grand Rectifier of Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍遣將軍曹義宗逼荊州，詔穆為使持節、南征將軍、[8]都督南征諸軍事、大都督以援之。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan sent the general Cao Yizong to press Jing Province; an edict made Mu Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Campaigns South, [8] Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of the southern expedition, and Grand Commander-in-Chief to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan sent the general Cao Yizong to press Jing Province; an edict made Mu Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Campaigns South, [8] Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of the southern expedition, and Grand Commander-in-Chief to rescue it.

sentences.zh: 穆潛軍徑進，出其不意，至即大破之，生擒義宗送闕。

translations.literal: Mu advanced his army by a secret route straight forward, taking the enemy unawares; on arrival he defeated them at once, captured Yizong alive, and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Mu advanced his army by a secret route straight forward, taking the enemy unawares; on arrival he defeated them at once, captured Yizong alive, and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 以功遷衞將軍，進封趙平郡開國公，增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was transferred to General of the Guard and advanced to Duke of Zhao Commandery with an increased estate of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was transferred to General of the Guard and advanced to Duke of Zhao Commandery with an increased estate of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 遷使持節，加侍中、車騎將軍、假儀同三司、前鋒大都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, made Palace Attendant, General of the Chariots and Cavalry, Acting with the same privileges as the Three Excellencies, and Grand Commander-in-Chief of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Bearer of the Staff of Authority, made Palace Attendant, General of the Chariots and Cavalry, Acting with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, and Grand Commander-in-Chief of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 與大將軍元天穆東討邢杲，破平之。

translations.literal: Together with the Grand General Yuan Tianmu he campaigned east against Xing Gao and defeated and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the Grand General Yuan Tianmu he campaigned east against Xing Gao and defeated and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 時元顥內逼，莊帝北幸，顥入京師。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Hao pressed from within; Emperor Xiaozhuang traveled north in fortune; Hao entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Hao pressed from within; Emperor Xiaozhuang traveled north in misfortune; Hao entered the capital.

sentences.zh: 穆與天穆既平齊地，回師將擊顥。

translations.literal: Mu and Tianmu, having already pacified Qi, turned their army to strike Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Mu and Tianmu, having already pacified Qi, turned their army to strike Hao.

sentences.zh: 穆先驅圍虎牢，盡銳攻之。

translations.literal: Mu as vanguard besieged Hulao and attacked with all his elite troops.
translations.idiomatic: Mu as vanguard besieged Hulao and attacked with all his elite troops.

sentences.zh: 將拔，屬天穆北渡，既無後繼，人情離沮，穆遂降顥。

translations.literal: When it was about to be taken, Tianmu crossed north; with no rear support, hearts were estranged and discouraged, and Mu then surrendered to Hao.
translations.idiomatic: When it was about to be taken, Tianmu crossed north; with no rear support, hearts were estranged and discouraged, and Mu then surrendered to Hao.

sentences.zh: 以河陰酷濫事起於穆，引入詰讓，出而殺之，時年五十三。

translations.literal: Because the cruel excess at Heyin originated with Mu, he was brought in for reproach and, on leaving, was killed; he was then fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Because the cruel excess at Heyin originated with Mu, he was brought in for reproach and, on leaving, was killed; he was then fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，追贈侍中、司徒公，諡曰武宣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to the palace he was posthumously appointed Palace Attendant and Duke of the Ministry of Works, with posthumous title Wuxuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to the palace he was posthumously appointed Palace Attendant and Duke of the Ministry of Works, with the posthumous title Wuxuan.

sentences.zh: 長子慶遠，永安中，龍驤將軍、青州開府司馬。

translations.literal: His eldest son Qingyuan, in the Yong'an era, was General of the Dragon Charger and Secretariat Marshal of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Qingyuan, in the Yong'an era, was General of the Dragon Charger and Secretariat Marshal of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 第二子孝遠，襲。

translations.literal: His second son Xiaoyuan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Xiaoyuan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 天平中，叛入關西。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he defected and entered Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianping era he defected and entered Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 孟威，字能重，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Meng Wei, styled Nengzhong, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Wei, styled Nengzhong, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 頗有氣尚，尤曉北土風俗。

translations.literal: He possessed considerable spirit and integrity and especially understood the customs of the northern lands.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed considerable spirit and integrity and especially understood the customs of the northern lands.

sentences.zh: 歷東宮齋帥、[9]羽林監。

translations.literal: He served successively as Director of the Eastern Palace Fast, [9] and Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Director of the Eastern Palace Fast, [9] and Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 時四鎮高車叛投蠕蠕，高祖詔威曉喻禍福，追還逃散，分配為民。

translations.literal: At that time the Gaoche of the Four Garrisons rebelled and fled to the Rouran; Gaozu ordered Wei to explain fortune and calamity, recall those who had scattered in flight, and assign them as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Gaoche of the Four Garrisons rebelled and fled to the Rouran; Gaozu ordered Wei to explain fortune and calamity, recall those who had scattered in flight, and assign them as commoners.

sentences.zh: 後以明解北人之語，敕在著作，以備推訪。

translations.literal: Later, because he clearly understood the languages of the northern peoples, he was ordered to serve in the Compilation Office to be available for inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because he clearly understood the languages of the northern peoples, he was ordered to serve in the Compilation Office to be available for inquiry.

sentences.zh: 永平中，自鎮遠將軍、前軍將軍、左右直長，加龍驤將軍，出使高昌。

translations.literal: In the Yongping era, from General Who Pacifies the Distance, Forward General, and Left and Right Direct Attendants, he was additionally made General of the Dragon Charger and sent as envoy to Gaochang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongping era, from General Who Pacifies the Distance, Forward General, and Left and Right Direct Attendants, he was additionally made General of the Dragon Charger and sent as envoy to Gaochang.

sentences.zh: 還，遷城門校尉、直閤將軍、沃野鎮將。

translations.literal: On returning he was appointed Commandant of the City Gates, General of the Direct Gate, and Garrison Commander of Woye.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was appointed Commandant of the City Gates, General of the Direct Gate, and Garrison Commander of Woye.

sentences.zh: 正光初，蠕蠕主阿那瓖歸國，詔遣前郢州刺史陸希道兼侍中為使主，以威兼散騎常侍為副，遠畿迎接。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguang, when the Rouran ruler Anagui returned to the state, an edict sent the former Inspector of Ying Province Lu Xidao as chief envoy with Acting Palace Attendant, and Wei as deputy with Acting Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry to welcome him from afar.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguang, when the Rouran ruler Anagui returned to the state, an edict sent the former Inspector of Ying Province Lu Xidao as chief envoy with Acting Palace Attendant, and Wei as deputy with Acting Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry to welcome him from afar.

sentences.zh: 阿那瓖之還國也，復以威為平北將軍、光祿大夫，假員外常侍，為使主護送之。

translations.literal: When Anagui returned to his country, Wei was again made General Who Pacifies the North and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Extraordinary Regular Attendant, as chief envoy to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: When Anagui returned to his country, Wei was again made General Who Pacifies the North and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Extraordinary Regular Attendant, as chief envoy to escort him.

sentences.zh: 前後頻使遠蕃，粗皆稱旨。

translations.literal: Before and after he was repeatedly sent to distant borderlands and in the main all accorded with the court's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after he was repeatedly sent to distant borderlands and in the main all accorded with the court's intent.

sentences.zh: 復加撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was again made General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，除大鴻臚卿，尋加驃騎大將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the Putai era he was appointed Grand Master of the Imperial Stud; soon after he was additionally made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the Putai era he was appointed Grand Master of the Imperial Stud; soon after he was additionally made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 天平三年卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianping he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianping he died.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、侍中、本將軍、都督冀瀛滄三州諸軍事、司空公、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, to his former generalship, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Ji, Ying, and Cang provinces, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Palace Attendant, confirmed in his former generalship, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Ji, Ying, and Cang provinces, Duke of the Ministry of Works, and Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 子恂嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xun inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 威弟季，稍遷鎮遠將軍、左中郎將、廷尉監。

translations.literal: Wei's younger brother Ji was gradually promoted to General Who Pacifies the Distance, Left Commandant of the Center, and Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's younger brother Ji was gradually promoted to General Who Pacifies the Distance, Left Commandant of the Center, and Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 以本將軍除廣州刺史。

translations.literal: With his former rank he was appointed Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: With his former rank he was appointed Inspector of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 預尒朱榮義舉，封鉅鹿縣開國公，食邑一千戶。

translations.literal: He took part in Erzhu Rong's righteous rising and was enfeoffed as Duke of Julu County with an estate of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in Erzhu Rong's righteous rising and was enfeoffed as Duke of Julu County with an estate of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 除撫軍將軍、廷尉卿，轉司農卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and Director of the Court of Justice, then transferred to Director of the Directorate of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and Director of the Court of Justice, then transferred to Director of the Directorate of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 出為平西將軍、華州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈車騎大將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：羅結枝附葉從，當舊之眷，子孫顯祿，俱至公王，伊馛以勇力見擢，而能贊伐姑臧之策，請參中祕之官，世祖嘉之於前，良有以也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Luo Jie's branch and leaves flourished; he enjoyed the favor of the founding house; his descendants held eminent salaries and all reached the rank of duke or king. Yi Bo was promoted for his courage and strength and could support the plan to campaign against Guzang and request participation in the secretariat; Shizu praised him beforehand—there was good reason.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Luo Jie's branch and leaves flourished; he enjoyed the favor of the founding house; his descendants held eminent salaries and all reached the rank of duke or king. Yi Bo was promoted for his courage and strength and could support the plan to campaign against Guzang and request participation in the secretariat; Shizu praised him beforehand—there was good reason.

sentences.zh: 乙瓌之驍猛，和奴之貞正，苟頹之剛直，虎子之威強，宇文之氣幹，咸亦有用之士。

translations.literal: Yi Gui's fierceness, He Qinu's uprightness, Gou Tui's stern rectitude, Huzi's awesomeness, and Yuwen Fu's force of spirit were all likewise useful men.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Gui's fierceness, He Qinu's uprightness, Gou Tui's stern rectitude, Huzi's awesomeness, and Yuwen Fu's force of spirit were all likewise useful men.

sentences.zh: 費穆出身致力，遂有功名，而末路一言，禍被簪帶。

translations.literal: Fei Mu from his origins devoted his strength and thus had fame and achievement, but one word at the end brought disaster upon his girdle and cap.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Mu from his origins devoted his strength and thus had fame and achievement, but one word at the end brought disaster upon his girdle and cap.

sentences.zh: 校之文和，異世同咎。

translations.literal: Compared with Wenhe, it is the same fault in a different age.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with Wenhe, it is the same fault in a different age.

sentences.zh: 其死也幸哉！

translations.literal: His death was fortunate!
translations.idiomatic: His death was fortunate!

sentences.zh: 孟威致力荒裔，其勤可錄矣。

translations.literal: Meng Wei's devotion to the remote borderlands—his diligence is worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Wei's devotion to the remote borderlands—his diligence is worth recording.

translations.idiomatic: Advanced to king and again made commander of the western route: all editions lack the three characters "wang you wei"; the Beishi, juan 25, Yi Gui biography has them.

translations.idiomatic: Fought with the Left Director of the Route Song Xian: all editions have "Zong" for "Song".

translations.literal: According to the matter, see the Beiqishu, juan 20, Song Xian biography.
translations.idiomatic: According to the matter, see the Beiqishu, juan 20, Song Xian biography.

translations.literal: The character "Zong" is erroneous; now changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The character "Zong" is erroneous; now changed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 高宗初 諸本「高宗」作「高袓」，北史卷二五和其奴傳作「文成」。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wencheng's reign: all editions have "Gaozu" for "Gaozong"; the Beishi, juan 25, He Qinu biography has "Wencheng".
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Wencheng's reign: all editions have "Gaozu" for "Gaozong"; the Beishi, juan 25, He Qinu biography has "Wencheng".

translations.literal: Li Ciming and Zhang Senkai both say "Gaozu" should be "Gaozong".
translations.idiomatic: Li Ciming and Zhang Senkai both say "Gaozu" should be "Gaozong".

translations.idiomatic: as seen in juan 36, the biography of Li Shun with appended biography of Li Fu.

translations.idiomatic: Li Hui is in the Outer Kinship Biographies, Part 1, juan 83; he was killed by Empress Dowager Feng.

translations.idiomatic: The Suishu, juan 27, Offices Treatise, Central, Northern Qi, Under the Gate Department, has "Bureau of Fast Directors, four Fast Directors, in charge of laying out furnishings and sweeping."

translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi surely followed the Wei system.
